articles.title: Peugeot E-208 GTi: es el heredero del 205 GTi y conducirlo te da un subidón
articles.standfirst: Cuarenta años después del primer 205 GTi, Peugeot resucita sus siglas más deportivas en un 'juguete' eléctrico con el que no dejas de pasarlo bien.
articles.summary: Cuarenta años después del primer 205 GTi, Peugeot resucita sus siglas más deportivas en un 'juguete' eléctrico con el que no dejas de divertirte.
articles.body: Adaptarse a la conducción por el norte de Glasgow (Escocia), a donde hemos ido a conducir por primera vez el nuevo Peugeot E-208 GTi, requiere adaptarse a algunas dificultades. Las carreteras, a menudo estrechas, serpentean entre cambios de rasante y giros cerrados, entre montañas cuya cima cubre la niebla, mientras al volante debes andar con cuidado para que los 345 Nm de par instantáneo que libera su motor eléctrico te dejen cubrir cuanto antes esos adelantamientos en los que tú no decides el momento (conduces por la izquierda con coches con volante a la izquierda), sino un copiloto en el que debes tener confianza 'ciega'. Todo ello añade un punto de emoción cuando se trata de volver a enfrentarte a unas siglas históricas. El 205 GTi debutó en marzo de 1984, en el Salón de Ginebra, con un motor 1.6 de 105 CV que entonces parecían un vendaval de potencia. Cuatro décadas más tarde, y obligado por los tiempos que corren, el testigo pasa a un motor eléctrico. El salto puede hacer torcer el morro a los más puristas, pero reconforta saber que detrás de su desarrollo ha estado Peugeot Sport, el brazo deportivo de la marca y responsable del 9X8 del Mundial de Resistencia, que ha tratado de resolver esta metamorfosis sin traicionar el espíritu original. Los pasos de rueda ensanchados, la nueva parrilla con la triple garra iluminada que se extiende hasta los faros de LED y las preciosas llantas de 18 pulgadas (inspiradas en las históricas ruedas 'agujereadas' del 205 GTi), ya componen una estampa que se aleja lo suficiente del E-208 convencional. Pero contribuyen también el difusor trasero en negro brillante, el spoiler delantero específico y los toques de rojo repartidos por la parrilla, las pinzas de freno, los plásticos que cubren los pasos de ruedas guardabarros y las siglas GTi en el pilar C. Todo queda agresivo, muy fiel a lo que vimos en el primer prototipo (se presentó el 13 de junio en la víspera de las 24 Horas de Le Mans), pero sin caer en excesos. La paleta de colores se compone de siete tonos, entre los que destaca el Miramar Blue, pero a nosotros nos gustan sobre todo los Elixir Red y Okénite White porque son los que más recuerdan al 205 GTi . Dentro, el rojo vuelve a ser protagonista. Hasta descubrimos que las alfombrillas son de este color, mientras nos planteamos lo poco que tardaríamos en comprar unas genéricas en negro para no manchar las de serie. El tono rojo se repite en cinturones y costuras del salpicadero, en puertas, en asientos (con una línea inspirada en la que llevaba el 205 GTi 1.9) y en el volante, que cómo no es muy compacto. A este le queda muy bien su cuero perforado con Alcantara en las zonas superior e inferior, mientras la instrumentación digital adopta un tema más rojizo con visualizaciones específicas de rendimiento. Pero entre uno y otra no hay levas para modificar la retención del motor, lo que enfría un tanto el entusiasmo que al principio nos invade. Pulsamos el motor de encendido, movemos el pequeño selector a la D... y el coche sale con la misma discreción sonora que desearíamos si lo estuviéramos robando. Un único motor eléctrico montado en el eje delantero entrega 281 CV y los citados 345 Nm de par, cifras impropias de un coche que cualquier profano podría confundir con un simple utilitario. El software de gestión electrónica procede de forma directa de los programas de competición de Peugeot Sport y se ha optimizado hasta lograr la relación potencia-peso más favorable de su categoría: 5,5 kg por CV. El resultado se traduce en un 0 a 100 km/h de 5,5 segundos, dos décimas menos de lo previsto en la propuesta inicial, respaldado por un 0 a 1.000 metros en 25,8 segundos y una capacidad de recuperación de 80 a 120 km/h que se resuelve en 3,2 segundos. La velocidad máxima, como en casi todo eléctrico, no te permite presumir tanto porque se queda en 180 km/h. Como era de esperar, hay modos de conducción: Normal, Eco y Sport. Sus diferencias no afectan a sonido (artificial, no muy agresivo y con capacidad de desconexión), dirección ni en suspensión. Pero al menos sí que se notan, y bastante, en cómo se incrementa y aviva la respuesta en Sport, al igual que se contiene y limita en Eco. La batería es la misma unidad de 54 kWh brutos (51 kWh útiles) del E-208 convencional, aunque su gestión térmica ha sido reescrita por completo para soportar las exigencias del motor GTi. Los ingenieros han aplicado a la refrigeración los conocimientos sacados de competición, ajustando cuánto refrigerante circula y en qué momento según la temperatura, para evitar limitaciones de potencia incluso en circuito o subiendo un puerto de montaña a 'ritmos enérgicos'. Claro está que rodar así no permite acercarse a la autonomía prometida, que llega a 375 km con neumáticos Hankook Ventus S1 Evo3, sin coste adicional, o se queda en 352 km con los Michelin Pilot Sport 4S de serie. La recarga al completo se resuelve en 4 horas y 40 minutos en un wallbox de 7,4 kW, o en menos de media hora del 20% al 80% si encontramos un cargador rápido de 100 kW. La tecnología 'se palpa' cuando ves que el sistema i-Connect Advanced cuenta con navegación conectada TomTom, control por voz (hay que decir "OK Peugeot") y conectividad con Apple CarPlay y Android Auto. Pero hay más: la aplicación MyPeugeot permite el preacondicionamiento remoto de la temperatura y programar horarios de carga, y ofrece un planificador de rutas que optimiza autonomía y paradas de recarga y función Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) para usar la batería del coche para alimentar dispositivos externos. Todo ello queda respaldado por una garantía de hasta 8 años o 160.000 kilómetros, tanto para el coche como para la batería, y por el pase Free2Move Charge, con acceso a cerca de un millón de puntos de recarga repartidos por Europa. Pero la atención no debe detenerse demasiado en la electrónica cuando vuelves a sentarte en un GTi, en este caso con una carrocería rebajada en 25 milímetros respecto al E-208, unas vías ensanchadas 56 milímetros delante y 28 detrás y unas llantas de 18 pulgadas calzadas con neumáticos 215/40 R18. En su lugar, tratas de centrar toda tu atención en el empuje que sientes en tu espalda (muy poderoso, pero no espectacular), en un volante que ofrece la dureza justa... También en unas suspensiones firmes, más incluso de lo que uno esperaría de un pequeño GTi. De hecho, delante monta una barra estabilizadora de 17 mm y detrás otra de 31 milímetros, al tiempo que equipa muelles específicos y topes hidráulicos de recorrido, una tecnología tomada del programa WEC de Peugeot Sport. El resultado es un giro sorprendentemente plano, a lo que contribuye que los 340 kg que pesa la batería están bajo ese precioso suelo enmoquetado en rojo que pisamos. Y, para que después de frenar antes de cada giro y mantener tracción durante la curva este GTi no se desboque al salir de la misma (a menudo los tramos de carreteras estaban muy húmedos), la tracción se apoya en un diferencial autoblocante mecánico que reparte la potencia muy bien incluso con poca adherencia. Porque, traccionar tracciona muy bien. Tanto, que nos hubiésemos animado a poner el ESP en modo Sport para divertirnos más, si no fuera porque circular al revés sobre el mojado asfalto escocés no hace demasiado conveniente venirse arriba. Insistimos: buscándole un poco las cosquillas, echamos en falta unas levas para modificar la retención, que puestos a pedir fueran grandes y de tacto sólido. Si en un GTi se trata de sentir emoción al volante, y teniendo en cuenta que el paso a lo eléctrico puede suponer para los más 'quemados' un bajón (a pesar de que las prestaciones son magníficas), estas levas nos harían sentir más dueños de la conducción y más dominadores del coche. Pero tampoco su carencia echa por tierra el resultado final. En cuanto a los frenos, los discos delanteros han crecido hasta los 355 mm y cuentan con pinzas de cuatro pistones (pintadas en rojo), mientras en el eje trasero los discos son de 268 mm, al igual que en el E-208. Frenar, frena muy bien, aunque con un tacto esponjoso que no está a la altura de la deportividad que transmiten el empuje o las suspensiones. El E-208 GTi ya está a la venta. Su precio se ha fijado en 41.800 euros antes de ayudas, lo que hará que no prolifere en exceso y que cada vez que veamos uno por la calle sintamos el deseo de seguirlo con la mirada.

articles.title: Virat Kohli passes 15,000 ODI runs as India beat West Indies
articles.summary: Kohli remained not out on 139 off 88 balls as the hosts romped to an eight-wicket win in their first ODI of the series.
articles.body:
Virat Kohli has become only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar to reach 15,000 runs in men’s one-day international (ODI) cricket, achieving the milestone with an unbeaten century as India cruised to an eight-wicket victory over West Indies.

Kohli struck 139 not out from 88 balls and Shubman Gill made 110 as India chased down 296 with 50 balls to spare to take a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series on Sunday.

The milestone comes just days after Kohli announced that he would retire from national duty after next year’s 50-over World Cup. The leading century-maker in ODIs has already retired from T20 internationals and Test cricket ⁠⁠and now represents India only in the 50-over format.

Rohit Sharma and Gill launched the chase with a 74-run opening stand before Sharma was dismissed in the 12th over. Gill, the world’s top-ranked ODI batter, then took control, maintaining the aggressive approach and bringing up his 10th ODI century with a sweep.

Kohli came in at number three and notched his 86th international century, while Gill struck 110 in 108 deliveries as the pair put on a dominant 151-run stand off 132 balls that all but sealed the contest on Sunday.

Roston Chase eventually removed Gill, but Ruturaj Gaikwad made 13 off 19 balls and helped Kohli steer India home without further alarm. Kohli sealed victory with successive boundaries.

Put in to bat after the toss, Justin Greaves and John Campbell gave the West Indies a strong start, adding 135 from 117 balls for the opening wicket.

India struggled to find a breakthrough for much of the first 20 overs as the pair dominated the bowling and provided a solid platform.

Greaves, who was dropped by Sharma on 16, made India pay with a maiden ODI century and top-scored for the visitors.

The momentum shifted when Kuldeep Yadav dismissed Campbell in the 20th over, beating him in the air as he swept a catch to short fine leg. Yadav and Prasidh Krishna then applied the brakes on the West Indies innings as they lost four wickets for 22 runs between the 31st and 36th overs.

Yadav finished with 4-40 on his ODI return, but Amir Jangoo counterattacked with 58 off 43 balls. With support from Chase, he helped the West Indies recover from 198-5 and post 295.

articles.title: Esha Singh wins individual silver in women’s 25m pistol at Asian Games 2026 after missing team event medal
articles.summary: Esha Singh battled through multiple shoot-offs before finishing with a silver medal in the women’s 25m pistol at the 2026 Asian Games, adding another
articles.body: Esha Singh battled through multiple shoot-offs before finishing with a silver medal in the women’s 25m pistol at the 2026 Asian Games, adding another individual medal to her Asian Games record.The world No. 1 and world-record holder finished the final with 38 hits, the same score as China’s Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won gold. Esha’s 4+2 record in the shoot-offs left her second, while Xiao finished with 4+3.Esha’s route to the podium was far from straightforward. After the elimination stages, she was involved in an intense battle with South Korea’s Kim Hyon Suk for third place. Esha had to negotiate three shoot-offs against the Korean before securing her place in the medal positions.She then had to go through two more shoot-offs against Xiao to determine the gold and silver medals. Xiao eventually prevailed, leaving Esha with silver.Asian Games Full Coverage|Medal Tally|ScheduleEsha began the final strongly, scoring 5, 4 and 3 in the first three series. She then added 4, 4, 3, 3, 5, 3 and 4 across the remaining seven series.Kim, who eventually took bronze, finished with 34 hits, while Vietnam’s Trinh Thu Vinh was fourth with 30. China’s Shang Kaiyan finished fifth with 24.The silver adds to Esha’s record at the Asian Games. At the 2023 Hangzhou Games, she won silver in the individual 25m pistol and gold in the team event.At the ongoing Games, Esha had earlier missed out on a medal in the women’s 25m pistol team event, with India finishing fifth.Her medal also adds to India’s shooting haul at the Nagoya Asian Games, with the country continuing to pick up medals across individual and team events. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Pincky Balhara wins her second Asiad medal, adds kurash bronze to 2018 silver
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s Pincky Balhara secured her second Asian Games medal in kurash, clinching bronze in the women’s -78kg category after losing 0-5 to South
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s Pincky Balhara secured her second Asian Games medal in kurash, clinching bronze in the women’s -78kg category after losing 0-5 to South Korea’s Sumin Mo in the semifinals at Aichi-Nagoya on Monday.The 27-year-old thus added another medal to her Asian Games collection, eight years after winning silver in the women’s -52kg category at the 2018 Jakarta Games, when kurash made its debut at the continental event.Balhara’s latest podium finish also marked India’s third medal in kurash at the Asian Games. The Indian had reached the semifinals with a 3-0 victory over South Korea’s Garam Lim in the quarterfinals.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleBalhara’s second Asiad podium finishBalhara began her campaign in the quarterfinals against Lim, where she secured a convincing 3-0 victory to book her place in the last four. The Indian produced the decisive score through a ‘Chala’, a scoring move awarded when a competitor throws an opponent but does not demonstrate complete control over the action.Lim, meanwhile, failed to register a point during the contest, allowing Balhara to progress to the semifinals and put herself in contention for another Asian Games medal.However, the Indian could not overcome Mo in the semifinals. The South Korean secured a 5-0 win, ending Balhara’s hopes of reaching the final and leaving her with the bronze medal.Mo earned a ‘Yonbosh’ point during the contest, while Balhara was penalised with a ‘Dakki’. The Indian was unable to recover from the disadvantage as the South Korean controlled the bout to seal her place in the final.From Jakarta silver to Aichi-Nagoya bronzeBalhara first made her mark at the Asian Games in 2018, when she won silver in the women’s -52kg category in Jakarta. Kurash was introduced to the Games programme that year, giving Indian athletes an opportunity to compete for medals in the Uzbek martial art.Her silver medal was among India's early successes in the discipline, and her latest podium finish underlines her continued presence in the sport at the highest continental level.The Indian contingent added another medal through Balhara’s performance on Monday, taking its overall tally at the Games to 39, comprising four gold, 17 silver and 18 bronze medals.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Javi Leal y Fran Guerrero: una llamada que dice muchas cosas
articles.summary: La opinión de Jesús Mata
articles.body: Hay gestos que duran un segundo, pero que cuentan una historia entera. El de Javi Leal y Fran Guerrero después de ganar el FIP Platinum de Lyon fue uno de ellos. Mano con pulgar y meñique extendidos, como quien hace una llamada, algo que podía parecer una celebración más o una simple ocurrencia después de levantar un título, pero llegaba después de una semana demasiado larga para ellos y el mensaje parecía bastante más evidente: aquí estamos. Venían de quedarse fuera del Mundial después de haber entrado en la prelista, después de haber alimentado el sueño, lógico y legítimo, de vestir la camiseta de España en una cita de tal calibre. Y quizá por eso, cuando llegó la victoria, decidieron responder de la única manera que un deportista sabe hacer mejor: compitiendo y ganando. ¿Puede alguien interpretar aquel gesto como una falta de respeto hacia Juanjo Gutiérrez? Por supuesto. Cada uno puede leerlo como quiera. Pero personalmente prefiero quedarme con otra lectura, una que creo que le hace bastante más bien al pádel y que, estoy seguro, es la que hace el propio seleccionador: la de dos jóvenes que se llevaron un golpe, que no estuvieron de acuerdo con el desenlace y que, en lugar de esconder la frustración debajo de la alfombra, salieron a la pista con ganas de demostrar que tenían motivos para creer en ellos mismos. Y eso me gusta. Me gusta que los jóvenes tengan carácter. Que les duela quedarse fuera y que no les dé igual. Porque a veces parece que al deporte le pedimos a las nuevas generaciones que sean demasiado correctas, demasiado pacientes, demasiado maduras demasiado pronto. Que acepten una decisión, agachen la cabeza, sigan trabajando y esperen su turno. Y sí, claro que hay que saber aceptar las decisiones, respetar a quien las toma y aprender de ellas, pero también hay algo profundamente deportivo en mirar al otro lado de la red y decir: ya verás. Esto, bien entendido, creo que es necesario. Y más en una generación a la que muchas veces hemos señalado precisamente por lo contrario. Se ha hablado mucho de los jóvenes del pádel, y en ocasiones con razón, de sus comportamientos, de sus prioridades, de cómo gestionan determinados momentos, de esa exposición permanente que les acompaña casi desde que empiezan a despuntar. Han cometido errores y seguirán cometiéndolos, porque también forma parte del proceso de convertirse en deportistas de élite. Porque debajo de todo ese ruido hay jugadores que quieren ganar, que tienen hambre y que se enfadan cuando pierden. Que sienten que una oportunidad perdida escuece, que una convocatoria que no llega duele cuando llevas tiempo soñando con ella y que, cuando las cosas no salen como esperaban, todavía tienen esa capacidad tan necesaria en el deporte de apretar los dientes y volver a la pista. Leal y Guerrero ya no podían cambiar la decisión de Juanjo, pero sí podían decidir qué hacer con esa rabia. Canalizaron todos esos sentimientos y los proyectaron sobre la pista de pádel en Lyon. Como debe ser. En Londres, meses atrás, después de aquella derrota en primera ronda y tras llegar de Sudáfrica, donde habían alcanzado la final, una discusión viral que escondía una frustración se convirtió entonces en algo que no ayudó a nadie. Yo, optimista por naturaleza, pensé en su momento que también de esas situaciones se aprende... y creo que ha sucedido. A veces será cara y a veces será cruz, pero no creo que al pádel haya que quitarle esa sangre. Creo que hay que enseñar a los jóvenes a utilizarla, a convertir el enfado en entrenamiento, la decepción en ambición y las ganas de demostrar en resultados. Porque hay algo tremendamente sano en un deportista joven que, después de recibir un golpe, no se resigna y responde compitiendo. El límite está ahí, pero la llamada queda y, aunque no haya obtenido respuesta, seguro que Juanjo esbozará una sonrisa cuando lo vea.

articles.title: Asian Games: How a rare, inexplicable miss by Rahi Sarnobat cost India a 25m pistol team medal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India were left ruing a costly and extraordinary lapse by experienced shooter Rahi Sarnobat after a rare miss in the women’s 25m pistol team
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India were left ruing a costly and extraordinary lapse by experienced shooter Rahi Sarnobat after a rare miss in the women’s 25m pistol team event derailed their medal hopes at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya on Monday. Sarnobat’s shot yielded zero points in the fourth series, a setback that proved decisive as India finished fifth, outside the medal positions.The Indian trio of Esha Singh, Manu Bhaker and Sarnobat combined for a score of 1727-56x in the team competition. China won gold with 1743-68x, while South Korea (1735-65x) and Chinese Taipei (1734-48x) took silver and bronze, respectively.For Sarnobat, a former Asian Games gold medallist, the incident was particularly difficult to explain. The shooter herself admitted that she had never experienced anything similar in her career."This is the first time that something like this has happened in my career and I do not know how it happened," Sarnobat said.Her unexpected zero in a competition where every shot counts left India with little room to recover and turned what could have been a medal-winning performance into a disappointing fifth-place finish.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleHow one miss changed India’s medal prospectsThe women’s 25m pistol event featured both team and individual competitions, with India fielding three experienced shooters in Esha, Manu and Sarnobat. While Esha kept India’s hopes alive in the individual event, the team’s medal ambitions took a major hit during the qualification rounds.Sarnobat endured a difficult fourth series, registering a score of just 39. The series consisted of five shots, and her performance included the rare miss that resulted in zero points. The setback was particularly damaging in a tightly contested competition, where the margin separating the medal-winning teams was relatively small.Sarnobat eventually finished 30th in the individual qualification standings with a score of 568-16x. Her teammates also had contrasting fortunes in the individual event. Esha qualified for the final in eighth place with 580-22x, while Manu narrowly missed out, finishing 11th with 579-18x.India’s final team score of 1727-56x left them 7 points behind bronze medallists Chinese Taipei and just 8 points behind silver medallists South Korea. The gap to the gold-winning Chinese team was 16 points, underlining the impact of the team’s missed opportunities.Sarnobat, who won gold in the women’s 25m pistol at the 2018 Asian Games in Jakarta, was among India’s most experienced competitors in the discipline. Her admission that she could not explain the unusual mistake added to the disappointment of a campaign in which India had entered the event with medal aspirations.Esha Singh salvages an individual silverWhile India missed out on a team medal, Esha produced a determined performance in the individual event to secure silver after an exceptionally long final.The 21-year-old from Hyderabad, the reigning world number one, fought through five shoot-offs, including three to move into medal contention and two more in the gold-medal contest against China’s Xiao Jiaruixuan.Both shooters finished regulation with scores of 38, forcing another shoot-off to decide the winner. Esha faltered on the final shot, allowing Xiao to take gold by a single shot. North Korea’s Kim Hyon Suk claimed bronze after losing her shoot-off against Esha, finishing with 34 points."Yes, I was under pressure and this is the longest match of my career so far. My arms were aching at the end of it," Esha said after the final.For Manu, meanwhile, the Asian Games ended without an individual medal. The two-time Olympic medallist had already finished fifth in the women’s 10m air pistol event and was unable to qualify for the 25m pistol final.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Bélgica vs Francia
articles.standfirst: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Bélgica y Francia en el Stade Roi Baudouin correspondiente a la jornada 2 del Grupo 1 de la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.summary: 1XBET te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Bélgica y Francia en el Stade Roi Baudouin correspondiente a la jornada 2 del Grupo 1 de la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.body: Bélgica afronta esta segunda jornada de la Nations League con la confianza que supone haber comenzado la competición con una prestigiosa victoria a domicilio. El conjunto dirigido por Mark van Bommel se estrenó con triunfo ante Italia en el Olímpico de Roma. Un resultado que permitió al técnico neerlandés debutar de la mejor manera posible en el banquillo belga. Ahora, tendrá que confirmar esas buenas sensaciones ante uno de los grandes favoritos al título en busca del liderato en solitario. Favorito para el partido entre Bélgica y Francia Francia también inició con buen pie la Nations League después de imponerse a Turquía a domicilio. Zinédine Zidane tuvo así un estreno victorioso al frente del combinado galo... aunque la alegría quedó parcialmente empañada por la lesión de Kylian Mbappé. El delantero francés marcó el único gol del encuentro, pero tuvo que abandonar la concentración y regresar a Madrid. Las casas de apuestas conceden el favoritismo a los visitantes: 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 3.84 por la victoria de Bélgica, 4.04 por el empate y 1.83 por el triunfo de Francia. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una opción interesante en las apuestas deportivas. Especialmente, después de los resultados de ambas selecciones en la primera jornada. Bélgica consiguió imponerse a Italia manteniendo su portería a cero, mientras que Francia hizo exactamente lo mismo en su visita a Turquía. Los dos combinados demostraron solidez defensiva en sus respectivos estrenos... aunque el potencial ofensivo de ambos puede cambiar esta tendencia en un duelo de mayor exigencia. 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 1.49 por el 'sí' y de 2.47 por el 'no'. Número total de goles (Over/Under) La línea de goles también parte de una estadística idéntica para Bélgica y Francia. En la victoria belga frente a Italia se marcaron menos de 2.5 goles totales, mientras que el triunfo francés ante Turquía también se resolvió sin superar esta barrera. Ambos encuentros terminaron con marcadores ajustados, aunque el enfrentamiento directo entre dos selecciones con tanta capacidad ofensiva puede presentar un escenario diferente. 1XBET paga a 1.50 que se superen los 2.5 goles y a 2.39 que se registren menos de 2.5 tantos. Último equipo en marcar El mercado del último equipo en marcar presenta una tendencia favorable a ambos conjuntos después de sus respectivos estrenos. Bélgica fue capaz de anotar el último gol en su victoria ante Italia, mientras que Francia hizo lo propio frente a Turquía gracias al tanto que decidió el encuentro. La igualdad en este aspecto contrasta con el favoritismo general de los visitantes, que parten con una cuota más baja para volver a ser el último equipo en marcar. 1XBET ofrece una cuota de 2.41 por que Bélgica marque el último gol y de 1.61 por que lo haga Francia.

articles.title: Asian Games: Priya, Lovlina storm into semifinals as India’s boxers continue to assure medals in Aichi-Nagoya
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India’s boxing campaign continued to gather momentum at the Asian Games 2026 as Priya Ghanghas and Lovlina Borgohain powered into the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India’s boxing campaign continued to gather momentum at the Asian Games 2026 as Priya Ghanghas and Lovlina Borgohain powered into the semifinals on Monday, assuring the country of two more medals in the ring. The duo’s victories added to an already growing list of Indian boxers who have reached the last four, underlining the sport’s contribution to India’s medal haul in Aichi-Nagoya.Lovlina, the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist, produced a commanding 5-0 unanimous-decision victory over South Korea’s Seong Suyeon in the women’s 75kg quarterfinal. The win guaranteed the Assam boxer at least a bronze medal and a second successive Asian Games podium finish after her silver at Hangzhou in 2023.Priya followed with another 5-0 victory, overcoming Tajikistan’s Mijgona Samadova in the women’s 60kg quarterfinal to book her place in the last four.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleLovlina assures second successive Asiad medalCompeting in her first bout of the tournament, Lovlina made an aggressive start against Seong, repeatedly using her jab-cross combination to unsettle the South Korean. Although Seong attempted to use her height advantage and landed a barrage of punches in the second round, Lovlina’s movement and cleaner combinations kept her in control.The Indian continued to find openings with her crosses and hooks before finishing strongly with quick 1-2 combinations. The judges awarded her all three rounds, giving her a comprehensive 5-0 victory.For Lovlina, the medal continues an impressive run across major international competitions. She won silver at the previous Asian Games and also claimed Commonwealth Games silver last month, adding to medals won at the World Championships, Asian Championships and World Cup.Lovlina will face Kazakhstan’s reigning 70kg world champion Natalya Bogdanova in the semifinal.Priya joins growing list of Indian semifinalistsPriya, the Asian Championship gold medallist and reigning Commonwealth Games champion, also secured her place on the podium with a unanimous decision against Samadova.Her progress means India now have multiple boxers assured of medals, with Parveen Hooda (65kg), Ankush Panghal (80kg) and Narender Berwal (+90kg) having already entered the semifinals on Sunday.Parveen defeated Uzbekistan’s World Championships silver medallist Navbakhor Khamidova 5-0, while Ankush recorded a similar unanimous-decision win over Tajikistan’s Nekruz Salimov. Narender also advanced to the last four in the +90kg category.India had returned from the previous Asian Games with four boxing medals, including one silver and three bronze. With the competition still having several rounds to go in Aichi-Nagoya, the Indian boxing contingent has already positioned itself for another significant contribution to the country’s medal tally.Kapil Pokhariya is also in action on Monday in the men’s 90kg quarterfinal, giving India another opportunity to add to its growing list of semifinalists.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Last-minute dash, accomodation chaos, weight cut attempt: How Varun Sanyal's Asian Games nightmare unfolded
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: By the time Varun Sanyal finally reached his room in Nagoya, nearly 12 hours had passed since landing in Japan.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: By the time Varun Sanyal finally reached his room in Nagoya, nearly 12 hours had passed since landing in Japan. He had flown from London to Mumbai, collected his Asian Games accreditation card, travelled via Singapore, spent hours proving he was a registered athlete, and then found himself sharing a room that wasn't meant for three people.A few days later, he was lying outside a sauna, hyperventilating after collapsing during a weight cut attempt that ended his Asian Games campaign before it had begun.Yet Sanyal, who has now returned to London, would rather remember the Asian Games as the moment mixed martial arts (MMA) forced itself into India's sporting conversation."Instead of focusing on what didn't happen, you focus on what did," he said in a conversation with TimesofIndia.com, referring to teammate Suchika Tariyal's historic bronze medal — India's first Asian Games medal in MMA.For a sport making its Asian Games debut, that perspective may prove more significant than his own heartbreak.A fighter who almost wasn't thereSanyal's road to the Games was anything but straightforward.The 26-year-old had earned qualification months earlier, but uncertainty over selection meant he shifted his attention back to his professional MMA career. Ranked among Asia's top six, he was eventually drafted into the Indian squad only two weeks before the Games after another athlete became ineligible under the Sports Ministry's selection criteria.Those two weeks became a race against time.He was recovering from a staph infection, reorganising an international training camp in England, arranging travel documents, and attempting to shed nearly five kilograms to make the lightweight limit — all while preparing for what should have been the biggest tournament of his career.On paper, Sanyal arrived in Nagoya as one of India's brightest MMA prospects. The Delhi-based fighter had already built an impressive résumé across amateur, semi-professional and professional circuits, compiling 17 bouts in just four years and establishing himself as one of the country's most active competitors. But nothing in that experience prepared him for the chaos that awaited off the cage.The Games before the GamesThe accommodation chaos became one of the defining stories of Aichi-Nagoya 2026, and Sanyal finds a mention in that storyline.His name was missing from the registration list upon arrival. Officials at the Expo Hall directed him to the cruise ship that served as the Athletes' Village, where another round of explanations began from scratch. Questions over whether he was even registered followed, despite the accreditation card that had allowed him into Japan. The issue was eventually resolved only after intervention from the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), but not before an entire day had disappeared.The logistical mess exposed a deeper problem for Indian MMA.I just remember that I finally hit the 30-minute mark and I stood up. And when you're dehydrated, you start seeing black, like you're starry-eyed. You get that head rush. I was completely out of it. I push the door to the sauna, and then there's this tiny bench, which I just flat out start lying down on, and I'm hyperventilating. Honestly, this whole thing feels like a fever dream.Unlike many established sports, the MMA contingent travelled without coaches being granted accreditation inside the cruise. Some of the coaches paid for their own flights, hotels and transport, while the athletes were left to manage themselves inside the village.That meant Sanyal wasn't simply preparing to compete. He became translator, manager and teammate rolled into one.He helped Suchika navigate anti-doping procedures, searched the sprawling cruise ship for medical assistance and even sprinted between decks looking for an iron to prepare India's competition kits.In another sport, those responsibilities would belong to support staff. In India's newest Games discipline, they fell to the athletes themselves.30 minutes of chaos inside the saunaIf the accommodation saga tested Sanyal's patience, the weight cut attempt tested his body.Competing in the 77kg category is slightly misleading. Because athletes weigh in wearing a gi and belt weighing around 1.5kg, competitors effectively need to reach roughly 75.5kg. Sanyal normally walks around at 80kg and had managed to cut down to 77.5kg before the final cut.Two kilograms remained and the clock was ticking down.Inside the sauna, the first few minutes were almost routine. Fighters from Kyrgyzstan, Singapore and Brunei chatted casually while everyone sweated through the final stages of preparation. Then dehydration began taking over.Sanyal remembers measuring time only through the sauna clock — one checkpoint after another. Around the 30-minute mark, he stood up, experienced a severe head rush and stumbled onto a nearby bench before collapsing.I have cut weight before and made it to the tournaments, so that wasn't the challenge. I think it was the short time window accompanied with all the stress, travel, etc. Plus just not having anyone there."I just remember that I finally hit the 30-minute mark and I stood up. And when you're dehydrated, you start seeing black, like you're starry-eyed. You get that head rush. I was completely out of it. I push the door to the sauna, and then there's this tiny bench, which I just flat out start lying down on, and I'm hyperventilating. Honestly, this whole thing feels like a fever dream," he said with a laugh.A Nepali athlete alerted his coach, who then attempted to communicate with Japanese medical staff through a translation app while Sanyal insisted, somewhat irrationally, that he did not want water because he still needed to make weight."My body was really overheated at this point. I felt like I had a fever. I said I need to speak to my coach. Fortunately, the person near me was Nepali, so my coach spoke to him in Hindi. They then took me to a medical facility. There, my coach asked them to give me electrolytes. They spoke in Japanese and with limited English. Meanwhile, I am out of it and still saying not to give me anything because I am trying to cut weight."Eventually, doctors treated him for dehydration and overheating, and medical advice to rehydrate immediately meant his Asian Games campaign officially ended.Looking back, Sanyal thinks it wasn't the smartest decision to cut weight. Doing it alone, after frantic travel and with virtually no recovery time, only added to the risk."I have cut weight before and made it to the tournaments, so that wasn't the challenge. I think it was the short time window accompanied with all the stress, travel, etc. Plus just not having anyone there. I think had I done it in a more systematic way while I was there in the sauna, maybe."I don't want to speculate because then I start thinking of what could have been. And then it becomes a bit frustrating," he explained.The medal that changed MMA's India storyWhile Sanyal recovered, Suchika Taiyal won a bronze medal and became the first Indian MMA athlete to stand on an Asian Games podium. Sanyal had been in her corner throughout the competition — not officially as a coach, but as the closest thing India had inside the village.Her medal, coming controversially, altered the conversation.For years, MMA in India has largely existed outside the mainstream sporting ecosystem, thriving in independent promotions while fighting for institutional recognition. The Asian Games offered legitimacy, and the medal offered proof that the country could compete with Asia's best.Sanyal believes that is the real legacy of Nagoya.The federation (MMA-SFI) itself is barely over a year old, yet India has already produced medals at the Asian Youth Games and now the senior Asian Games. For a discipline only just entering the multi-sport landscape, those results matter as much as infrastructure.His own story, strangely enough, helped too.The accomodation controversy, the viral videos that went with it, the failed attempt at playing the continental showpiece brought unprecedented attention to a sport that rarely finds itself on front pages. It wasn't the publicity he wanted, but perhaps it was the publicity Indian MMA needed."We still came away with a medal despite everything going on, which I think is huge. Two things to this. The medal showing that we (can) produce results. The federation that sent us has only been in existence for just a little over a year or so. And even at the Asian Youth Games, medals were produced. So I'd say the biggest takeaway is that the federation and the athletes have shown that MMA fighters can produce results. Now I would like the government, the corporate sponsors and the audience to get behind the MMA fighters," said Sanyal."If you ask my personal takeaway, I'm glad that there was so much interest shown. It was at my expense but the fact of the matter is so much media attention went on the sport, put on the athletes and for that I'm grateful. So for me that that's the biggest takeaway," he continued.Sanyal left Nagoya without stepping into the cage. Yet in many ways, his toughest fight had already been won: convincing an entire country that MMA belongs on its biggest sporting stage.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vuelve Madrid Horse Week porque “¿a quién no le gusta Ben-Hur?”
articles.standfirst: Tras un año de ausencia y de la mano de Mutua, reaparece el evento multidisciplinar ecuestre más importante de España, con tres Copas del Mundo, doma, saltos y, la gran novedad, enganche
articles.summary: Tras un año de ausencia y de la mano de Mutua, reaparece el evento multidisciplinar ecuestre más importante de España, con tres Copas del Mundo, doma, saltos y, la gran novedad, enganche
articles.body: Después de un año sin celebrarse por problemas burocráticos y de financiación, vuelve Madrid Horse Week, el evento multidisciplinar ecuestre más importante que se celebra en España. Lo hace a lo grande, de la mano de Mutua Madrileña, con la celebración del 26 al 29 de noviembre en los pabellones 12 y 14 de Ifema, de tres Copas del Mundo, las de doma, saltos y, la gran novedad, enganche. “Porque ¿a quién no le gusta un poquito de Ben-Hur?” Eso se preguntaba Daniel Entrecanales, el presidente del Comité organizador del evento ecuestre que nació en 2012 y que vuelve con más fuerza en 2026. “Después de la ausencia del año pasado hay una ilusión colectiva para que todo salga bien, hay más ganas que nunca”. En 2024, alrededor de 45.000 espectadores se acercaron a Ifema para disfrutar del evento multidisciplinar que en 2023 fue premiado por la Asociación de la Prensa de Madrid como el mejor de los celebrados en España. Está prevista la participación de más de 170 jinetes y amazonas de 20 países, cerca de 300 caballos y más de 40.000 metros cuadrados dedicados el universo ecuestre. Al acto de presentación, celebrado en la majestuosa explanada del Palacio Real, con un bello carruaje de enganche incluido, acudieron diferentes personalidades como Javier Revuelta, presidente de la Española de Hípica, que destacó “la importancia deportiva de este evento porque nuestros deportistas se medirán a los mejores del mundo meses antes de los trascendentales Europeos de 2027 que son clasificatorios para los Juegos”. Al margen de las tres competiciones de élite mundial y de su tradicional Concurso de Saltos Internacional, destinado a amateurs y jóvenes promesas del salto de obstáculos, Mutua Madrid Horse Week 2026 contará con el Salón del Caballo, con decenas de estands especializados en productos hípicos, equipamiento técnico, moda ecuestre, complementos, alimentación y servicios relacionados con el caballo, propuestas de 'lifestyle', gastronómicas y actividades para toda la familia. Los visitantes dispondrán de una programación ininterrumpida de exhibición y espectáculos ecuestres en la llamada Pista Non-stop. Las entradas se pueden comprar desde el 1 de octubre en la web del evento, madridhorseweek.com Almudena Maíllo, delegada de Turismo del Ayuntamiento de Madrid, y Luis Martín Izquierdo, viceconsejero de Cultura y Deportes de la Comunidad de Madrid, volvieron a resaltar el impacto de la capital como sede de los principales acontecimientos deportivos del mundo. “Madrid tenía ganas y le gusta Madrid Horse Week, por lo que la celebración de esta nueva edición es una magnífica noticia. Precisamente, en el Ayuntamiento de Madrid apostamos porque la ciudad no sólo tenga eventos puntuales, sino que el calendario esté lleno todo el año. En Madrid hay pasión por el deporte", recordó Maíllo. La fiesta, por otro lado, no sería posible sin Oxer Sport, representado por su presidente Álvaro Arrieta, y, sobre todo, por Mutua Madrileña. Ignacio Garralda, presidente ejecutivo de la compañía de seguros, explicó su apuesta fuerte por la hípica. “Queremos acercarnos a un deporte hermanado con la excelencia. Nos debemos a los madrileños. Estamos ‘condenados’ a estar en todo gran evento en la ciudad”.

articles.title: ‘We did not expect this from Japan’: Pakistan volleyball team taken to wrong venue as logistical woes mount at Asian Games
articles.summary: Pakistan’s volleyball team was taken to the wrong venue ahead of its crucial Pool A match against Uzbekistan at the Asian Games 2026, adding to growing
articles.body: Pakistan’s volleyball team was taken to the wrong venue ahead of its crucial Pool A match against Uzbekistan at the Asian Games 2026, adding to growing complaints over logistical arrangements at the multi-sport event in Aichi-Nagoya.Pakistan captain Murad Jehan took to Instagram to express his frustration after the team bus headed to the wrong gymnasium, leaving the players short of time before their match.“We have a very important match and the bus driver doesn't know which gymnasium we are going to play,” Jehan said in a video recorded on the bus.“He took a wrong way and came to a wrong gymnasium and now we are short of time. It's an embarrassing situation,” he added. “We did not expect this from Japan. This should not have happened.”Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleThe detour left the players with little time for their usual preparations before the match. According to Jehan, some members of the squad were forced to change into their playing kit while still on the moving bus.‘This is not the only mismanagement’Jehan said the venue mix-up was part of wider logistical difficulties that athletes had encountered during the Games.“Really disappointing situation. This is not the only mismanagement that athletes are facing here,” he said.The Pakistan captain also complained about food availability, saying meals were not always available to athletes at dining areas after training sessions.The Games organisers did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on the volleyball team's complaint.Despite the disruption, Pakistan managed to put the incident behind them once they reached the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Gymnasium. They defeated Uzbekistan 3-0 to secure their second successive victory in the competition.The episode came just days after the Games' chief organiser apologised for widespread logistical glitches. Organisers attributed some of the problems to an unexpected late influx of around 2,000 additional athletes and team officials, which had put pressure on operational planning.Rain adds to scheduling headachesThe logistical concerns came as persistent rain created another set of problems for organisers on Monday, disrupting competitions across several sports.The men's cricket quarterfinals involving Pakistan and Hong Kong and India and Afghanistan were both washed out after heavy rain left the playing surface at Korogi Athletic Park unplayable. With no reserve day built into the schedule, Pakistan and India advanced to the semifinals on the basis of their higher rankings.Afghanistan opener Mohammed Akram expressed his disappointment after his side's match against India was abandoned.“The rain started yesterday, so hard luck for us,” Akram said. “We would have been happy to play here with India – our players are in form.“But unfortunately the rain has ruined everything.”Tennis matches were also delayed, while surfing was called off because of poor wave conditions. India's Kishore Kumar Anbarasu managed to complete his heat before the surfing programme was abandoned, advancing to the quarterfinals.“It was not the easiest conditions. It was very hard to find the good waves,” Anbarasu said.With the Games running until October 4, organisers face further weather-related challenges, with Typhoon Surigae forecast to move towards central Japan and the Tokyo region later in the week.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
