articles.title: Ranking the Top 10 Funniest Athletes
articles.summary: New York Knicks point guard Jalen Brunson spent Saturday night doing something he's never done on a basketball court: trying to make America laugh.
articles.body:
New York Knicks point guard Jalen Brunson spent Saturday night doing something he's never done on a basketball court: trying to make America laugh.

Fresh off leading the Knicks to their first NBA championship in 53 years and winning Finals MVP, Brunson took the stage to host the Season 52 premiere of Saturday Night Live . In his opening monologue, he brought in Knicks teammates Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart and turned his late-game reputation into a punchline. He also starred in a memorable High School Musical parody sketch.

Brunson's SNL debut is a reminder that the line between professional athlete and entertainer has never been particularly rigid. Some athletes have breakout roles in TV and film comedies, some use social media better than a Gen Z brand manager, and some are simply gifted with natural off-the-cuff timing or deadpan delivery.

It's difficult to rank athletes' comedy chops because they all shine in different ways. Kevin Durant is a grade-A troll. Peyton Manning is the ultimate character actor. Shaquille O'Neal uses his size to his advantage with physical humor and slapstick comedy.

Still, we persist. Here is our ranking of the 10 funniest athletes ever to grace our screens, courts and fields.

Honorable Mention: Tom Brady (Unintentionally Funniest Athlete)

Some athletes are funny because they're working hard at it. They star in Hollywood films or host SNL . Others are naturally funny, shining when they clap back on social media or drop a non sequitur on live TV.

Meanwhile, Tom Brady has produced his funniest moments when he is not actively trying to be funny. In fact, Brady's form of humor might be termed anti-comedy. During his entire career, he painstakingly built a public persona as the most committed, serious and competitive guy in the room (any room; pick a room).

But in the vein of Michael Scott, Brady's combination of self-seriousness, earnestness and obliviousness often make him the funniest person in the room, even if he doesn't realize it.

There is an exception: If you can get Brady to relax, you can get some genuinely incredible moments out of him. The ultimate example is the Bucs' 2021 championship parade, where Brady, spurred on by several shots of tequila , made an underhand toss of the Lombardi Trophy from his moving boat to another moving boat. Thankfully, tight end Cameron Brate caught the pass.

The highest compliment for any funny person is that they don't have to work at it; it's inherent in their nature. That's definitely the case for New York Knicks shooting guard Josh Hart, whose willingness to be the butt of the joke and genuine oddball personality naturally translate to comedy.

Off the court, Hart might be best known for co-hosting The Roommates Show podcast alongside teammate Jalen Brunson and longtime friend Matt Hillman. Using Step Brothers as a blueprint, The Roommates Show is meant to evoke an off-the-cuff dorm-room hang. Hart never hesitates to poke fun at himself, whether it's his hairline or lack of "freak athleticism."

Hart loves a good bit, and one of his best ones was his yearlong campaign to convince fellow Villanova Wildcat Mikal Bridges to join the Knicks. Hart continually pestered Bridges on X , and when Bridges came on to the podcast, Hart removed his hoodie to reveal a Knicks shirt underneath . When Bridges finally joined the Knicks in a blockbuster June 2024 trade, Hart celebrated as if he had been the one to offer the term sheet (and somehow avoided a fine for tampering).

Hart's constant trolling of Brunson's "big head" has also turned Knicks postgame press conferences into appointment television.

Natural comedic talent is all well and good, but WNBA star Sydney Colson has taken it a step further as a student of the medium.

Colson has taken classes in stand-up comedy in preparation for a career as a comedian and actress following her playing days. She even performed a live set at "Fever Fest" during the WNBA's 2025 All-Star Weekend. Colson also treats the arrivals tunnel as an open mic, complete with physical comedy (at times both intentionally and unintentionally tripping).

Sometimes, humor is about more than making people laugh. Colson's Indiana Fever teammate, Caitlin Clark, has praised Colson for her ability to lighten the mood during tougher moments.

Before joining the Fever in 2025, Colson was known for her witty and zany bench antics with then-Las Vegas Aces teammate A'ja Wilson.

Preseason Contenders in Desperation Mode

Though he was billed as a brooding powerhouse ("The Animal") during his WWE career, the signs that Dave Bautista would be a natural comedian were already there. His persona involved taking everything literally, theatrical dramatics and sometimes unhinged tantrums, which played well against characters such as John Cena's fan-favorite babyface.

But after Bautista left WWE (the first time) in 2010, his comedic chops really started to develop. He took on what would become his breakout film role as Drax the Destroyer in 2014's Guardians of the Galaxy , which he reprised in five more Marvel films between 2017 and 2023. (See: "I'll do you one better: Why is Gamora?")

His role as an aggro Twitch streamer in Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery in 2022 allowed him to blend WWE acting and screen acting into a perfect comedic vessel. Off the big screen, Bautista displays his deadpan, dry wit when he replies to internet comments .

A Twitter/X All-Star, Kevin Durant toes the delicate line between obnoxious and hilarious that is inherent to trolling, which by all accounts is one of his favorite pastimes.

It doesn't matter whether you're a former teammate or an anonymous egg (remember those?) with 12 followers. There's a good chance Durant will jump into your mentions and roast you mercilessly.

There are too many gems to list here, but the Hall of Fame moments from early in Durant's career (c. 2009–10) include the hot take that " Twitter is better than goin to da club ," getting robbed by a dog , struggling with bubble guts , wanting to drink Scarlett Johanssons bath water and being unable to believe what he was seeing when he saw a girl in the club (da club) with a duffel bag for a purse .

As the years have gone on and KD's follower count has soared over 20 million, he has kept his innermost thoughts closer to the vest. But you'll still find him trolling fans and media members in equal measure.

On one hand, no list of the funniest athletes of all time would seem complete without LeBron Jame. On the other hand, you'll find detractors from Redditors to Stephen A. Smith terming his particular brand of humor "corny," dismissing him for trying too hard and being too earnest.

It all comes down to your taste. After all, not all comedy is for everyone.

There's no denying LeBron is a ham. He embraces the role, and has done so in everything from roles in feature films like Trainwreck to hosting SNL . In the latter role, he was completely down to do self-owning sketches like "LeBronologue," a parody of his own Nike commercial.

You will never not find LeBron committing to the bit . If he just toned down the skits that turn out to be commercials and sponsorships, he would certainly win over some of his detractors.

Coming up in WWE alongside Dave Bautista, John Cena was likewise destined to blossom into a bonafide comedian. During his wrestling career, he was known for his out-of-the-box insults of rivals like The Rock and Roman Reigns and charming the crowd with his wholesome hero persona.

But if the world at large didn't know just how funny John Cena (a true "full name on every reference" person) could be, he welcomed the chance to prove it when he took his talents to Hollywood.

Like LeBron, Trainwreck was John Cena's entry point to mainstream comedy. Since starring as Amy Schumer's unnervingly intense boyfriend in 2015, he has gone on to flourish in films like Daddy's Home , Sisters , The Suicide Squad and Barbie , while arguably becoming as well-known for his role as Peacemaker as for his legendary WWE career.

One could feasibly put the top four of these rankings in any order and not be wrong. Some would undoubtedly argue Marshawn Lynch deserves the No. 1 slot, as he has leaned into the comical contrast between his public persona and actual personality and made it his trademark.

It all started with "I'm just here so I won't get fined" at Super Bowl media day, a bit which became so famous that he registered it as an official trademark in 2015. Lynch developed a reputation for being difficult with the media, racking up more than $1 million in fines for skipping press conferences during his career.

But as Marshawn revealed more of his true personality in appearances on Conan , The League, Murderville and Xbox promos (Jericho forever), it became clear that if you allow Marshawn to be Marshawn on his own terms, the result is comedy gold.

His funny streak predates his NFL career, too. At Cal, he celebrated an overtime win by joyriding a medical injury cart around the field.

Inside the NBA isn't a studio show with some comedy; it's a comedy show with some basketball. Charles Barkley is to Inside the NBA as Ellen Pompeo is to Grey's Anatomy , having been at the heart of the show for more than 25 (!) years.

Having more than two decades to hone his comedic timing and develop recurring bits gives Barkley a clear advantage over other current and former athletes. However, it's also harder to be considered consistently funny over a long period of time. You have to prove it's a trait, not a fluke. And you undoubtedly develop more haters.

Enough intellectualizing; let's turn to the bits themselves. Barkley has had some incredible highlights over the years, although the women in San Antonio might beg to differ .

There was the time he attempted to break David Blaine's record of 7:08 minutes holding his breath underwater and failed by 6:44 . There were his short-sleeve button-up shirts and nearly falling asleep from boredom.

One of the funniest moments of Barkley's television career is the infamous bracelet story . It starts with Kenny Smith asking Barkley who made his bracelet and devolves into three minutes of sheer chaos.

Among everyone featured here, Shaquille O'Neal excels the most at slapstick comedy. At 7'1", he uses his size to his advantage.

If comedy is a study in contradictions, Shaq's enormous physical presence combined with his childlike antics is a recipe for success almost every time.

Shaq plays off Charles Barkley on Inside the NBA . During Barkley's infamous bracelet story, Shaq did a spit take before getting up and walking away from the set, wheezing, which in turn made Barkley's bit even funnier.

Other times, the big man has literally fallen off the set. As his "Shaqtin' a Fool" segment proves, Shaq has always been down for the bit.

Like many of the other athletes in these rankings, Shaq has shown off his comedy chops in TV and films such as Kazaam , Steel , Grown Ups 2 and Scary Movie 4 .

Like his longtime rival Tom Brady, Peyton Manning cultivated a reputation for being intense, hypercompetitive and self-serious. But Manning is self-aware enough to understand that it's objectively funny to apply that persona to situations that in no way warrant it.

The most famous example is the United Way sketch from when Manning hosted SNL in 2007. Frustrated that the kids he's playing with aren't living up to his expectations, he hurls expletives at them and beans them in the back of the head with the ball.

The bit was so outrageous that Manning initially refused to do it . Then one parent of a child actor allegedly ran over and said, "I want him to hit my kid in the face!" Then it was off to the races.

Manning may have the best natural comedic timing of any athlete on this list. He's not the type to throw everything against the wall to see what sticks; he's intentional and chooses his moments, meaning that he doesn't often miss.

While a legitimate argument could be made for anyone in this top four, we're handing the crown to Peyton.

articles.title: NHL Trade Ideas for Quinn Hughes to Teams That Aren't the Devils
articles.summary: The 2026-27 NHL regular season is here, and the Minnesota Wild still have not signed superstar defenseman Quinn Hughes to a long-term contract extension beyond this season.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 NHL regular season is here, and the Minnesota Wild still have not signed superstar defenseman Quinn Hughes to a long-term contract extension beyond this season.

That creates a pretty significant issue for the Wild.

They know he is an unrestricted free agent after this season, and if he were going to be signed to a new deal to keep him in Minnesota, you would have expected it to happen at some point over the summer.

The speculation around Hughes has been loud for more than a year now, and it always revolves around him trying to play alongside his brothers, Jack Hughes and Luke Hughes, with the New Jersey Devils .

If that speculation proves to be true, the Wild would have just one make-or-break season to try to win with him before losing him for nothing. Are the Wild good enough to take that sort of chance? Or would it be in their best interests to move him, recoup some value, and try to move forward with the return they get for him?

There's a good argument to be made for both.

The most likely option here, and the one I would choose if I were placing a bet on what the team does, is that Minnesota goes with the former and tries to win it all, risking whatever comes after that in free agency.

There just doesn't seem to be much urgency, at this point, to explore anything else. There might still be a hint of optimism that they can get him to re-sign (which might be the least likely of the three possibilities).

Maybe that changes as the trade deadline approaches.

Or if Minnesota's season goes in a direction no one is anticipating and fails to meet expectations.

So, for now, let's just play the "what if" game and explore the latter option, wondering what it might look like if Minnesota did pursue the trade.

And let's do something a little different and look at teams that are NOT the Devils, just because the assumption has always been the Devils. If the Wild were to move him at some point, Hughes has no trade protections in his deal and could theoretically be traded anywhere.

Why Would (or Should) the Wild do this, and What's the Value?

Teams hoping to be a contender do not typically trade players like Hughes, no matter the contract situation, because players like Hughes are often a key reason they ARE a contending team.

When the Wild acquired Hughes from the Vancouver Canucks midway through the 2025-26 season, they did so with the mindset that they would have at least two playoff runs with him and perhaps entice him to re-sign.

He has not re-signed. While every player has a price, there may not be a price within reason that will convince Hughes to bypass unrestricted free agency and the ability to choose his next destination.

As recently as two years ago, former Vancouver Canucks president of hockey operations Jim Rutherford was publicly speaking about Hughes' desire to play alongside his brothers. If Rutherford is saying something, you should listen, because he's one of the few people in a position of power in the NHL who has no filter between his brain and mouth and will always give you honest thoughts.

All of this puts the Wild in a tough spot for this season. Go all-in this season and see what happens with Hughes? Or move him?

The pro to going all in is that Hughes is one of the best players in hockey, and they have a better chance with him than without him, even if they were to move him for a return.

The con is that there is a good chance he leaves for nothing, while the Wild don't actually win it all. If Rossi or Buium (or both) become impact players in Vancouver, and Hughes leaves as a UFA and the Wild never get close to a championship, the whole thing could end up looking incredibly messy and ugly for the Wild.

As good as the Wild team is with Kirill Kaprizov, Matt Boldy, Hughes, Brock Faber, and the goalies, it's still a team that lacks the kind of big-time center depth (and even secondary winger depth) that championship teams require. It's probably on the second tier of Stanley Cup contenders. That's a good team. A very good team. But it might not be a Stanley Cup team. And they have to be realistic about that when it comes to handling the Hughes situation.

There is some precedent for a move like this.

Two years ago, the Colorado Avalanche traded superstar forward Mikko Rantanen, as a pending UFA, to the Carolina Hurricanes for Martin Necas, Jack Drury, and some draft picks. When Carolina realized it could not re-sign Rantanen, it moved him to Dallas for Logan Stankoven and two first-round picks.

We also have some sense of Hughes' trade value, given that he was dealt less than a year ago, bringing back Marco Rossi, Zeev Buium, Liam Ohgren, and a first-round pick.

His value would probably be lower than this season and would likely drop the closer it gets to the trade deadline, due to the limited term remaining on his deal.

So let's take a look at some teams that might have some interest in this.

Carolina has been burned by pending UFA's in the past, losing Jake Guentzel after acquiring him from the Pittsburgh Penguins, and then trading Rantanen before he even played 20 games in Raleigh. So there might be some hesitancy here to go all in on another one when everybody knows he's probably not staying.

But let's be illogical for a minute. Carolina is the defending Stanley Cup champion and has a very real chance of doing something special and going back-to-back. The team is that good. It has that good of a system. The coaching is that good. It is also a team that still has roughly $10 million in salary cap space and a cupboard full of draft pick capital, while also having some intriguing young talent that could be flipped.

Banners fly forever, and this is a contending team that might be able to afford taking an all-or-nothing, one-year risk to get a superstar on the back end of its defense.

The Capitals may have missed the playoffs in 2025-26, but on paper, everything about this team looks like a serious Stanley Cup contender, especially after a big offseason that saw them make some bold moves to acquire Jordan Kyrou, Alex Tuch and Boone Jenner.

They are one of the biggest teams in the league, have improved their transition offense, have an elite goalie, and are as deep as any other team. They can win, and they can win right now.

There is also probably some added urgency from the front office and ownership, given that Alex Ovechkin's playing future beyond this season remains in doubt. It seems likely that he will retire after this season, but nobody knows that for sure. It also seemed likely he was going to retire after the 2025-26 season. But here we are.

The Capitals reportedly had some interest in Hughes a year ago, but backed off when the asking price was too rich for their liking.

Would they revisit it this season if the opportunity presented itself? Not only because the price might be a little lower, but also because this team is better and has a much better chance of winning.

Even though Washington has significantly improved its roster and has an outstanding player in Jakob Chychrun at the top of its defense, it could probably use another top-four (or, in this case, top-pairing) defenseman to really bring everything together.

1 Prospect Every Team Can Get Hyped About 🤩

If the Wild did move Hughes before the deadline, you have to imagine they would focus on the Eastern Conference to avoid the risk of seeing him in the playoffs. Which is why I'm going with Eastern Conference teams in this exercise.

Carolina and Washington make sense as they should be Stanley Cup contenders, and absolutely have "win-now" vibes around them.

Montreal's a little different in that it should be a playoff team and likely will be one, but its Stanley Cup window of contention is only just starting to open.

The Canadiens could absolutely win this season, but they are better set up for sustained, long-term success beyond it. Especially as their core group is all locked into team-friendly contracts that should prove to be bargains against the ever-increasing salary cap in the coming seasons. They have the foundation to be a force.

But it is also a team that was in the Eastern Conference Final just this past season, and might see itself as having a chance to do something special right now.

A defense with Hughes, Lane Hutson and Noah Dobson would be as good of a top-three as there is in the Eastern Conference, or the entire NHL, and potentially help put them closer to the top.

If nothing else, it is a fun idea to think about.

articles.title: Predicting WWE Money in the Bank 2026 Winners, Surprise Returns and Bold Booking Calls
articles.summary: Money in the Bank is routinely one of WWE's most anticipated and unpredictable events of the year, and the 2026 installment emanating from New Orleans is shaping up to be no exception.
articles.body:
Money in the Bank is routinely one of WWE's most anticipated and unpredictable events of the year, and the 2026 installment emanating from New Orleans is shaping up to be no exception.

The fields for the men's and women's Money in the Bank Ladder matches are nearly complete and consist almost entirely of Superstars who have never held world title gold in WWE. Although there are a few favorites in both bouts, it isn't uncommon of the company to pull off a swerve with either winner.

The only other announced match as of now is Roman Reigns defending his World Heavyweight Championship against LA Knight, a man who is no stranger to shortcomings at the annual event. Reigns retaining feels like a foregone conclusion, but how it happens and the possibility of a shock ending can't be counted out completely.

Ahead of Money in the Bank 2026, let's look who's most likely to go over in each outing, surprise returns, bold booking calls, last-minute additions to the card and more.

Penta's exceptional performance against Roman Reigns for the World Heavyweight Championship on the Sept. 14 edition of Raw caused his stock to skyrocket and put him on a path to permanent main event status.

WWE followed up on his huge night in Mexico City by having him qualify for the men's Money in the Bank Ladder match one week later. He replaced Solo Sikoa and stole the win from Dominik Mysterio, who was heavily expected to not only be involved but also take home the briefcase.

Bron Breakker has been overlooked for some time and would be a great fit as Mr. Money in the Bank, but Penta securing the contract instead would hardly be a bad thing.

The former Intercontinental champion has had a standout 2026 and should further cement his status as a top-tier talent in WWE by earning a guaranteed shot at a world championship. He wouldn't necessarily have to cash in on Reigns, but he'd almost certainly have to cash in successfully to justify him holding the briefcase in the first place.

This year's men's Money in the Bank bout will be stockpiled with star power, so there's a number of direction directions WWE can go in with the winner, but Penta pulling out the victory would be the best possible outcome.

Stephanie Vaquer Defends and Retains the Women's World Championship

Paul "Triple H" Levesque has been keen on smaller cards for the premium live events and keeping them around three hours in length. Four or five matches is commonplace on most B-level shows in the modern era of WWE, so with only three officially announced for Money in the Bank, one would have to assume at least one more will be added before showtime.

An Undisputed WWE Championship defense from Sami Zayn could be in the cards or the expected rubber match between Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton, but it makes more sense for Stephanie Vaquer to defend her Women's World Championship at the event instead.

Vaquer vanquished Liv Morgan in her home country of Chile earlier this month and outright told Morgan and Becky Lynch on the Sept. 21 edition of Raw that they can get shots at her title. She never specified when that would be and whether it'd be in singles matches or in a Triple Threat.

The latter would be a logical way to further the feud between all three women, and if that does come to fruition, Vaquer must walk away still the Women's World champion. Morgan getting her rematch and losing would pave the way for Vaquer and Lynch to branch off into their own feud.

Solo Sikoa's Interference Inadvertently Costs LA Knight

LA Knight will come closer than he ever has before to becoming World Heavyweight champion at Money in the Bank when he battles Roman Reigns. While it isn't set in stone that he's losing, it's just difficult to fathom that WWE would give Knight Raw's top title temporarily before getting the belt back on Reigns in time for WrestleMania 43.

That would be the ideal direction for the final few months of the year, but WWE presumably isn't willing to upend their plans quite to that degree. If Knight is going to lose to Reigns yet again, there's bound to be some sort of shenanigans that come with it.

Knight has constantly acknowledged how it was The Bloodline as an entity that defeated him at Crown Jewel 2023, not just Reigns. The Bloodline hasn't been interfering in most of Reigns' matches this year, so they should let him go at it alone at Money in the Bank as well.

The 946, however, won't be as gracious. They already took out Solo Sikoa on the Sept. 21 edition of Raw and will surely have their sights set on costing Reigns his coveted championship come New Orleans.

Sikoa will reemerge to thwart their involvement, only to factor into the finish and inadvertently cause Knight to lose. Perhaps that will spark some tension between those two and even lead to Knight snapping on Sikoa if he believes he betrayed him on purpose.

Seth Rollins Addresses Absence, Latest Rumors on WWE vs. AEW and Worlds Collide Decision

Seth Rollins last wrestled at SummerSlam in a losing effort against World Heavyweight champion Roman Reigns. Their mini tribute to The Shield afterward was a fitting conclusion to their long-running rivalry, as well as a strong sendoff for Rollins ahead of his hiatus.

Upon returning from injury on the road to WrestleMania, Rollins had been so determined to settle his score with The Vision followed by rekindling his rivalry with Reigns that there wasn't an obvious plan in place for him post-SummerSlam. Thus, giving him some time away was the best thing WWE could have done with his character.

Rollins has been synonymous with not only the Money in the Bank briefcase but the event itself for his entire career, so an appearance at this year's installment would be appropriate.

It'd be better suited for a segment on the show, such as stepping up to Intercontinental champion Chad Gable or shutting up Big Cass or Dominik Mysterio, than interfering in Reigns vs. LA Knight or the men's Money in the Bank Ladder match.

A Rollins return at Money in the Bank would give fans an incentive to tune into Raw that Monday to see what he'll have in store.

Blake Monroe Steals a Spot and Wins Women's Money in the Bank

The sixth and final spot in the women's Money in the Bank Ladder match will be filled on Friday's SmackDown when Tatum Paxley, Tiffany Stratton and Candice LeRae collide in a Triple Threat qualifier.

That show will also see Blake Monroe (allegedly) make her main roster in-ring debut by finally facing off with Giulia, who she has been waging war with in backstage segments for months. Monroe should undoubtedly win that match, but what if that isn't the last time she's in action this weekend?

It doesn't happen all that often, but a precedent has been set for Superstars taking other people's spots in Money in the Bank Ladder matches by attacking them beforehand and going on to capture the briefcase (most notably Brock Lesnar in 2019).

Monroe could target Sol Ruca or Lola Vice, become Ms. Money in the Bank and then spend months teasing cash-ins on the champion of her choosing. WWE's use of the former NXT Women's North American champion thus far has been questionable, but she'd quickly turn her fortunes around if she were to shock the world by winning Money in the Bank without ever formally qualifying.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Seth Rollins Addresses Absence, Latest Rumors on WWE vs. AEW and Worlds Collide Decision
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Seth Rollins Planning to Return 'When the Time's Right'

How LA Knight Can Get Out of WWE Purgatory

Seth Rollins' last televised match was his loss to Roman Reigns at SummerSlam, though he took part in a tour of South America earlier this month.

In an interview with ESPN Chicago (via Jeffrey Harris of 411 Mania), the former world champion indicated he's happy to remain out of the spotlight for the time being.

"I'm just taking my time right now, kind of focusing on other things, and at the end of the day, you know, I'll come back when the time's right," he said. "I was able to go down to South America a couple of weeks ago and do some non-televised events for the South American and Mexican fans down there, and really fantastic crowds. I mean, just unbelievable."

Rollins went on to quip his next television appearance will be on NFL Network, rather than Monday Night Raw. He'll be on Good Morning Football with the Chicago Bears concluding Week 3's slate of action against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday night.

His comments provided some insight behind his absence as he's not currently nursing an injury. He appears to be simply taking a break from the ring.

Especially for somebody as tenured as Rollins, stepping away can be beneficial physically and help their on-screen character regain some freshness.

WWE Had Competitive Motive Behind Worlds Collide Broadcast Decision

Despite having a packed card headlined by Chicago native CM Punk, WWE declined to broadcast Worlds Collide live. Instead, a replay will air Wednesday.

Fightful Select reported the company attempted to undercut AEW's All Out show, which happened simultaneously in a different Chicago suburb.

"WWE sources admitted AEW sold better than they expected, though they were still happy with Worlds Collide sales," the report said.

AEW ultimately sold out Now Arena, and that was a point of pride for those within the promotion.

"I cannot tell you the pride that I feel because people did have a choice," AEW world champion Will Ospreay said in the post-show media scrum, per WrestlePurists . "And everyone that came to this show tonight chose the right company because we deliver the best pay-per-views, the best professional wrestling."

In one form or another, WWE has tried to eat into AEW's audience since the promotion launched in 2019. Having Worlds Collide in the same city on the same date as All Out was only the most recent example.

The Wrestling Observer Newsletter 's Bryan Alvarez (via Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News) reported this will remain a small part of WWE's programming and scheduling strategy.

Alvarez (via Mukherjee ) went on to say the next time could be on Oct. 6, when AEW is broadcasting Grand Slam France. That's the same night as NXT's weekly show.

The wrestling insider said it's "presumed NXT will have at least one big main roster."

Grand Slam France includes a title match between Ospreay and Kazuchika Okada. Chris Jericho will also wrestle Nick Wayne. Ospreay vs. Okada alone will be a big draw for fans.

Even if WWE brings out a marquee star or two, NXT may struggle to win the head-to-head ratings battle.

articles.title: A 42-year-old record, a trucker’s daughter: Vithya Ramraj breaks PT Usha’s mark and rewrites history
articles.summary: Vithya Ramraj had already made history by matching PT Usha's 42-year-old national record, and three years later, she finally broke it.
articles.body: Vithya Ramraj had already made history by matching PT Usha's 42-year-old national record, and three years later, she finally broke it.The 27-year-old Indian hurdler clocked a personal best of 54.75 seconds to win bronze in the women's 400m hurdles at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, breaking the national record that had belonged to legendary Usha since August 1984.In 2023, at the Hangzhou Asian Games, Ramraj had clocked 55.42 seconds to claim bronze and equal Usha's mark set at the Los Angeles Olympics on August 8, 1984. That record had stood for 39 years at the time.Asian Games Full Coverage|Medal Tally|ScheduleNow, in Nagoya, Ramraj went one better, shaving 0.67 seconds off the old national record en route to her second individual Asian Games 2026 medal.Her compatriot Anu Raghavan finished fifth in 55.88 seconds, also recording a personal best.The 26-year-old was part of India’s silver-medal winning mixed 4x400m relay team earlier in the Games, running the anchor leg and producing a strong finish to help India hold on to second place.The medal also adds to Ramraj's Asian Games record. She had won bronze in the women's 400m hurdles at the 2023 Hangzhou Games to go with to silver medals in the 4x400 relay and mixed events.A trucker’s daughter who refused to give upVithya grew up in a modest family, with her father working as a truck driver. Her mother enrolled Vithya and her twin sister Nithya, a 110m hurdler, at the Sports Development Authority of Tamil Nadu hostel in Erode. Athletics was not a carefully planned choice.“At a parent-teacher meeting, my PE teacher suggested sports for us. My mother chose athletics since it offered more visibility than team games. The sports hostel also helped, as my family couldn’t afford the expenses,” Vithya had told Times of India in 2025.After school, Vithya pursued a BBA degree under the sports quota and joined the national camp at NIS Patiala in 2018. But progress was slow. She later moved to Chennai in 2022, while a Covid infection and appendicitis surgery disrupted her preparations for the Tokyo Olympic trials.“In Patiala, I didn’t get personal training, struggled with the food, and didn’t know Hindi. While preparing for the Tokyo Olympic trials, I got Covid and later underwent appendicitis surgery. I had to leave camp and return home,” she had told Times of India.Her twin Nithya, who was training under coach Nehpal Singh Rathore, then helped bring Vithya into the setup. Until 2022, Vithya had primarily concentrated on the 400m flat, but Rathore encouraged her to pursue both events and set her sights on Usha’s record.The twins subsequently made history as the first pair of twins to represent India at the Asian Games. Vithya’s breakthrough at Hangzhou included three medals - bronze in the 400m hurdles and silver medals in the women’s 4x400m relay and mixed 4x400m relay - while her record-equalling run established her as one of India’s leading 400m hurdlers.Vithya’s rise continued after Hangzhou. She represented India at the Paris 2024 Olympics as part of the women’s 4x400m relay team, before adding another major international podium finish with bronze in the 400m hurdles at the 2025 Asian Athletics Championships in Gumi, South Korea.“The same villagers who once questioned our parents about sending us to Chennai for training are now celebrating us,” she had told Times of India.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Big blow for India! Defending champion Avinash Sable misses out on medal, finishes fourth in 3000m steeplechase
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India suffered a major disappointment in the athletics competition at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday as defending champion and Games record
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India suffered a major disappointment in the athletics competition at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday as defending champion and Games record holder Avinash Sable finished fourth in the men's 3000m steeplechase final, despite producing his season-best performance.Sable clocked 8:21.67 but could not reproduce the performance that had earned him gold at the previous edition. The Indian was unable to keep pace with the leading trio in a tightly contested final and eventually missed the podium.Japan's Ryuji Miura won the gold in a new Games record of 8:17.36, while compatriot Ryoma Aoki claimed silver with a personal best of 8:17.60. Qatar's Zakaria Elahlaami took bronze in 8:18.13.For India, Sable's fourth-place finish was particularly disappointing given his status as the defending champion and the Asian Games record holder in the event. His season-best 8:21.67 underlined his effort on the day, but it was still not enough to extend India's medal run in the men's steeplechase.Sable had emerged as one of India's most reliable athletics medal contenders in recent years, making the failure to finish on the podium a significant setback.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleVithya Ramraj breaks PT Usha's record, wins bronzeThere was, however, a historic moment for India in the women's 400m hurdles, with Vithya Ramraj producing a personal best of 54.75 seconds to win the bronze medal.The 28-year-old from Coimbatore finished behind UAE's Mariam Kareem, who won gold in a Games-record 54.31 seconds, and Kazakhstan's Adelina Zems, who took silver in a personal best of 54.58.Ramraj's performance also saw her surpass the more than four-decade-old national record held by legendary Indian athlete PT Usha. Usha had clocked 55.42 seconds at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.Usha, who now heads the Indian Olympic Association, was in attendance at the Games to witness the record being broken.The bronze was Ramraj's second medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games after she had earlier won silver in the 4x400m mixed relay. India's Anu Raghavan finished fifth in the final, setting another personal best of 55.88 seconds.Earlier, Commonwealth Games bronze medallist Seema Kaliramna also narrowly missed the podium in the women's discus throw final. articles.title: Eddie Hearn vs Dana White’s controversial beef explained and why it could wreck Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury finally appears to be set for December 11 in Cardiff after years of delays and failed negotiations.
articles.body: Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury finally appears to be set for December 11 in Cardiff after years of delays and failed negotiations. But the huge British heavyweight fight has been thrown into uncertainty because of a growing dispute between promoters Eddie Hearn and Dana White. White was named as part of the promotional team alongside Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh, creating an immediate problem for Hearn.Joshua’s contract reportedly prevents White and TKO Group from having involvement in the fight. Hearn has therefore opposed White’s role, while Alalshikh and White remain determined to be involved. The disagreement has now become a major threat to the fight, with Fury blaming Hearn’s “ego” and White accusing the Matchroom boss of hurting the event.How Eddie Hearn and Dana White’s relationship turned into a boxing warEddie Hearn and Dana White were once on good terms. Hearn had previously praised White and the Fertitta brothers for turning UFC into a global sports powerhouse. In 2020, Hearn even said he wanted boxing to adopt some of the UFC’s successful business model.The two promoters regularly communicated and even met at the UFC Performance Institute in Las Vegas. White also welcomed Hearn and Joshua cageside for UFC London in March 2022.Their relationship changed after White entered boxing with Zuffa Boxing. White and Alalshikh made it clear they wanted to challenge the established boxing promotions. Hearn welcomed the competition but also criticised TKO Group over its position on the Muhammad Ali Act.White later admitted he was surprised by Hearn’s reaction.He said, “I was actually surprised with Eddie Hearn at his - I’ve been cool with him for a long time - at his take on me getting into boxing and his reaction to it. Very negative, very confrontational, which I found weird because it’s not his style.”The rivalry became more personal when Zuffa signed Conor Benn. Benn had spent his professional career with Matchroom before signing a reported £11million ($14.5m) one-fight deal with White’s promotion. Hearn described himself as “DEVASTATED” by the move.Hearn then signed former UFC heavyweight champion Tom Aspinall to a commercial and advisory deal. White mocked the move and questioned what Hearn had done for the British heavyweight.That rivalry has now spilled directly into Fury vs Joshua. Hearn has objected to White being involved because of Joshua’s contract. White, meanwhile, insists he has a role in the event and says Hearn is damaging the fight.White said, “He hasn’t done the fight any favours. I don’t know anybody who is more full of s*** than Eddie Hearn.”Hearn has also accused White of trying to take credit for the fight after previously pushing for it to take place in America.White remains adamant about his involvement. He said, “I’m involved in the f***ing fight.”With Fury vs Joshua scheduled for December 11, the dispute has created serious uncertainty around the event. Fury has claimed there is now only a “ONE PER CENT” chance of the fight happening, while Alalshikh has indicated that he wants White and TKO involved.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Benjamin Satterley's Best Matches, Moments as AEW's Pac and WWE's Neville
articles.summary: The professional wrestling world was stunned Sunday evening when All Elite Wrestling announced the passing of Benjamin Satterley, better known as PAC, at the age of 40.
articles.body:
The professional wrestling world was stunned Sunday evening when All Elite Wrestling announced the passing of Benjamin Satterley, better known as PAC, at the age of 40.

An international superstar who experienced success across the independents, then in WWE and, finally, AEW, he was a revolutionary performer who flawlessly mixed unmatched athleticism with precise technical skill and was one of the wrestlers fans could trust to deliver every time he set foot inside the squared circle.

While memorializing a wrestler whose greatness was plentiful as his is nearly impossible, enjoy this trip through his undeniable career through some of his best matches and moments.

By the time the first NXT live event special, Arrival, aired on the brand new WWE Network, Satterley had found success as Adrian Neville and was more than ready to achieve his first major championship victory in pro wrestling's most prominent promotion.

After a year of coming up short, the Man Who Gravity Forgot defeated Bo Dallas in a Ladder Match to win the NXT Championship and cement himself as the face of the black and gold brand moving forward.

The victory, in front of a new audience of fans experiencing NXT for the first time, was a turning point for the brand, with one of the best wrestlers in the world now holding its championship.

Now the centerpiece of an entire roster, he would be trusted to carry NXT into the future and provide the audience with the exhilerating championship clashes at the top of the card that helped define everything Triple H and Co. wanted to accomplish with the revolutionary developmental product.

As Satterley's time in NXT drew to a close, there was one last thing needed of him: to put over Sami Zayn and pay off the beloved babyface's journey to championship gold.

He did just that on December 11, 2014, when the two clashed in what was the most hotly anticipated championship bout in NXT to that point.

A classic encounter between two stars who cut their teeth on the independents and in international competition, they wowed the NXT fans with high drama and incredible athleticism that concluded with Neville doing the selfless thing, enduring an exploder suplex into the corner, and a second Helluva Kick, as Zayn paid off his arduous journey and achieved a lifelong dream.

It was a legitimate Match of the Year candidate; one that may have defined Zayn's career to that point but, also, one that firmly established Neville as one of the best wrestlers in the world, a reputation he would carry with him to WWE's main roster.

His arrival on the main roster may have brought with it the loss of his first name and the ring gear of a modern-day superhero. Neville never allowed those changes to negatively influence his performance between the ropes.

Case in point: an August 3, 2015 match-up against WWE champion Seth Rollins in which he delivered the Red Arrow and nearly defeated The Architect in one of the great false finishes you will ever see.

Three months earlier, on the May 11 episode of Raw, he narrowly lost to John Cena in one of the franchise star's famous United States Championship Open Challenge matches.

In two extraordinary opportunities, against two of the best in the world, Neville proved himself capable of hanging with the top talent in WWE.

Teaming with Stephen Amell vs. Stardust and

With Stephen Amell, star of TV's Arrow , set to make his in-ring debut at the 2016 SummerSlam, WWE needed a Superstar it could trust to both carry the work rate of the match, as well as guide the non-wrestler should he get lost along the way.

Enter Neville, who accomplished both and as a result, what could have been a disastrous match on paper turned out to be a pleasant surprise.

In his biggest pay-per-view match to that point, the Man Who Gravity Forgot showed up, showed out, and earned the win for his team over the bizarre Stardust and reigning King of the Ring, Wade Barrett, pinning the latter with his jaw-dropping Red Arrow.

It was, to that point, one of the biggest wins of Neville's WWE run and, outside of his work to establish the cruiserweight division as a legitimate entity, one of the most important accomplishments of his career.

Despite being recognized by fans as one of the best in the world, creative frustration would lead to a messy divorce from the company. That separation, though, would open doors for him to compete elsewhere, such as an upstart company created by the man beneath the Stardust paint, Cody Rhodes.

The introduction of AEW gave wrestlers from around the world a true alternative to WWE, a promotion where they could excel by being among the best in the world.

Satterley wasted no time doing so, appearing under the name that had caught the attention of wrestling fans in the first place: PAC.

"The Bastard" targeted "Hangman" Adam Page first, defeating him on the debut episode of AEW Dynamite in October of 2019. Before that, at All Out that August, he earned a jaw-dropping win over Kenny Omega, forcing him to pass out in the clutches of the Brutaliser.

Those two programs would instantly elevate PAC in the eyes of the fans and confirm his status as one of the top wrestlers on the early AEW roster. The world had already known he was great, but those matches erased years of frustration and reminded the audience that he could be a legitimate world title contender, too.

It would be against an unlikely opponent that he would have the most important match-up of his AEW career.

On paper, Orange Cassidy stood no chance against The Bastard at AEW Revolution in February of 2020.

One was an admitted comedy act, while the other was a world-class competitor, one win away from the world title at any given point. With two differing styles, too, there was reason to believe fans were in for a car wreck of epic proportions.

What they got instead was a star-making match for Freshly Squeezed, thanks in large part to the extent that PAC was willing to put him over.

Overconfident, he shook off Cassidy's nonchalant nonsense and brutally beat him up for a large portion of the match. As things progressed and frustration over his inability to put his opponent away set in, the heel began succumbing to Cassidy's trademark offense and sold the tornado DDT better than anyone in company history.

The dramatic near-falls kept the fans in Chicago on the edge of their seats, believing they may witness a historic upset.

PAC inevitably downed Cassidy and tapped him out to the Brutaliser. Still, it was one of those star-making outings that saw him do everything in his power to put over Cassidy and his character in a big-match situation.

PAC would go on to have more technically sound bouts that looked the part of classics, but what he accomplished on that night, in front of a rabid crowd, earned him further respect from the AEW faithful and created a beloved babyface who would go on to become a sizeable star for the promotion.

PAC had experienced success in AEW before he joined up with Jon Moxley, Claudio Castagnoli, Wheeler Yuta, Daniel Garcia, and Marina Shafir in the Death Riders, teaming with Penta and Rey Fenix in Death Triangle.

With the Lucha Bros, he captured the AEW World Trios Championships and battled The Elite in an epic Best-of-Seven Series over the titles that saw them eventually drop the gold to Kenny Omega and the Young Bucks.

Injuries prevented that trio from having a satisfying ending, though.

Beginning in 2024 and running for the next two years, PAC's inclusion in the Death Riders meant he was at the forefront of some high-profile angles and matches, all while causing chaos, evoking toughness, highlighting his brutality, and backing up Moxley in his pursuit of championship domination.

He held back Wheeler Yuta, making the young star watch as his fellow Death Rider teammates maniacally attacked Bryan Danielson. He would routinely interfere on behalf of Moxley in his world title match-ups and, along the way, continue to showcase himself as one of the premier workers in the company, even as injuries often halted his momentum.

He represented that group in his final match on Saturday, September 26, when he battled Andrade El Idolo at All Out.

Another banger match between two NXT exports who left the mighty WWE to find success elsewhere, it was representative of PAC's pro wrestling career in that it set the tone in the opening match spot and further established his opponent as a world title contender.

Straight through until the end, everyone who worked with PAC was better for it, whether it was having a great match at a time when they needed it or being legitimized at a level they previously had not been.

A workhorse who always brought his best to the mat, that never changed during his entire stint with AEW.

Following the shocking revelation of his untimely passing, tributes to Satterley poured in across social media.

Reigning AEW World Champion Will Ospreay referred to PAC as England's greatest export, both as a wrestler and a person.

A heartbroken Kyle Fletcher recalled working with his hero.

WWE Raw general manager Adam Pearce expressed gratitude for the time he spent working with Satterley.

AEW referee Bryce Remsburg recounted the bond his children shared with their friend, Ben.

Finn Balor had one word to describe the great competitor: family.

AEW owner and president, Tony Khan, issued a statement on the passing of one of his company's foundational stars.

There are countless tributes similar to them across social media from the men and women who had the opportunity to know Satterley and work with him. They say less about his in-ring work as a wrestler and more about the man himself.

If a man's legacy is defined by the meaningful interactions he has had with those in his life, and will endure because of them, it is safe to say that the man who took so much joy in being a "Bastard" every Wednesday night on Dynamite was anything but.

articles.body:
Bleacher Report and WWE, part of TKO Group Holdings (NYSE: TKO), have reached a new multi-year content partnership that will bring WWE's biggest moments, Superstars and stories to B/R's massive global audience of sports fans.

Per the agreement, Bleacher Report will hold global highlight rights across WWE's programming slate, including Monday Night Raw , Friday Night SmackDown , NXT and WWE Premium Live Events such as WrestleMania ® , with content distributed across Bleacher Report, House of Highlights, B/R Wrestling — Bleacher Report's dedicated wrestling brand — and their associated social and digital platforms.

The partnership further expands Bleacher Report's industry-leading portfolio of content relationships across sports. B/R partners with the world's biggest leagues and properties including the NFL, NCAA, MLB, NHL and NBA, to bring fans closer to the favorite athletes, teams and moments. Adding WWE to its portfolio reflects B/R's broader strategy to serve fans across the full spectrum of sports and sports culture, particularly around properties that inspire passionate, year-round conversation.

Seth Rollins Addresses Absence, Latest Rumors on WWE vs. AEW and Worlds Collide Decision

Beyond highlights, Bleacher Report will have a ringside presence at select WWE PLEs, with B/R and House of Highlights content teams capturing original storytelling, talent-driven content and behind-the-scenes moments.

"WWE fans don't just watch. They are highly engaged, analyze every detail and debate the sport all week long. That's exactly the kind of passionate fandom B/R and House of Highlights were built for," said Bennett Spector, General Manager, Bleacher Report. "This partnership gives us the opportunity to bring fans closer to the biggest moments happening today while also tapping into the incredible history and personalities that have made WWE part of sports culture for generations."

"Bleacher Report has long been at the intersection of sports and culture," said Alex Varga, EVP, WWE. "Our partnership with B/R reinforces WWE's commitment to bringing our content to a global audience."

WWE coverage will begin rolling out across Bleacher Report and House of Highlights platforms leading into WWE Money in the Bank on Saturday, October 10.

articles.title: Can women become a much bigger part of the iconic America’s Cup?
articles.summary: When Louisa Nordstrom was growing up, the posters hanging in her bedroom didn’t portray pop stars or movie actors; instead, legendary British skipper Ben Ainslie was smiling from the wall, together with a dedicated autograph.
articles.body: When Louisa Nordstrom was growing up, the posters hanging in her bedroom didn’t portray pop stars or movie actors; instead, legendary British skipper Ben Ainslie was smiling from the wall, together with a dedicated autograph. Twenty years later, it is Nordstrom – now an accomplished sailor who’s training to race in next year’s America’s Cup – who hands out autographs to young women and girls looking for inspiration to follow her footsteps. “It’s a bit surreal,” Nordstrom says laughing to CNN Sports, before taking a more measured tone to reflect on her achievements. “I hope that young girls now are able to see more and more women at the highest level of sport and have something to aspire to and see that there is a path forward (in sailing).” Nordstrom and her ARC Team USA crew are in Naples this month to prepare for the 38th edition of the Cup, which will be held in Italy in July 2027. It will be the second European nation the world’s oldest still-running sports competition has visited (after Spain), but this year marks a historic first, with each team now required to field at least one woman as part of its crew. The inclusion of women, albeit mandatory, is no small matter, as sailing has long been accused of being a masculine environment, if not outright sexist. One survey published this year by The Magenta Project, 11th Hour Racing and World Sailing shows that three out of four women involved in sailing believe gender balance is a problem, while more than 85% of the women polled said they experienced sexism. “Sailing has historically been a very male-dominated sport and that’s the reality of it,” concedes Nordstrom, who believes however that the technological advances the sport has experienced in recent years has made it almost impossible to ignore calls for inclusions. “In a lot of sports, there are inherent biological differences between men and women, the unique thing now with sailing is that it’s becoming a more leveled playing field with regards to the physical capabilities (of the sailors),” she added. Tech advances equal the playing field Gone are the days of pulling ropes and lifting weights on the yachts. The AC40 and AC75 that Nordstrom trains with are fiberglass vessels where sails are lifted by hydraulic pressure and the route is analyzed by powerful computers. Jumping behind the steering wheel of one of the boats Nordstrom sails on feels like crawling into the cockpit of a race car rather than the cabin of an elegant yacht. On the left side, a series of buttons and automatic commands activate the lines to lift the sails, even in rough sea conditions. Nordstrom’s seat is within the hull of the boat, allowing only for the top of her head and eyeline to peek over and set the course – or half of it anyway. “The sail goes down in the middle of the boat, so when you’re sailing, you actually can’t see half of the racecourse, so you’re blind!” she says. Once at sea, cameras can only get a feeling of the real speed the AC40 is capable of as it foils past supporting boats and other vessels in an elegant breeze. “All of this signals an age of change where the physicality, that brute strength side of sailing that was so prevalent forever is, I wouldn’t say eliminated, but darn close,” Ken Read, one of the most successful sailors in US history and the CEO of ARC Team USA, tells CNN Sports. “It’s a lot more cerebral, and we all know women are smarter. Fitness is important, but mental capacity… I am often asked how does one get to be an America’s Cup sailor? I’d say stay in school and become an engineer,” says Read, who competed in two America’s Cups in 2000 and 2003. “You look at the boats I sailed in 2000 and then you look at these boats, and it’s a completely different animal. The sport of sailing has evolved more than any other.” A long history entering a new chapter The role of women is integral to that evolution because, decades before this year’s breakthrough, women have long been around the America’s Cup. In 1995, an almost-all-female crew led by Dawn Riley on board the Mighty Mary nearly managed to represent the US in the 1995 edition, a feat chronicled in a new documentary out this year of the same name. Seeing the Mighty Mary take on the male crews back then “was like watching Princess Leia take on Darth Vader,” a spectator to the event says in the film. Despite a valiant effort on the water, that milestone failed to normalize a more ever-present female presence at the Cup for almost three decades. Then in 2024, a new standalone event – the Women’s America’s Cup – was launched as part of the 37th edition in Barcelona, Spain, paving the way to the change in regulations and the mixed competition launched this year. Nordstrom and several of the athletes training in Naples when CNN visited took part in that event, which they think should be a mandatory step before climbing to the main competition. “(Female participation) should not come as mandatory,” says Shirley Robertson, a former Olympic sailor and presenter of CNN’s Mainsail program, who’s now working as a broadcaster for the Cup. “However, unless you mandate it, it would never happen. It took 32 years from Mighty Mary, but this year’s achievement is truly historic. This is a competition that means a lot to a lot of people… and there are a lot of traditions,” Robertson tells CNN Sports. For her part, Nordstrom shrugs off her achievement in the America’s Cup with a matter-of-fact attitude: “The goal, ultimately, is to have the best people on the boat, and now more than ever there’s more opportunities to gain that experience for females, so it should become level with time.” Nordstrom’s role as a sailor is not just limited to the Cup. Before the 2024 Women’s America’s Cup, she also competed in the qualifiers for the Paris 2024 Olympics in the 470 Class, a much smaller vessel composed of a mixed, two-person crew. With the Summer Games heading to Los Angeles in 2028, is that also on her mind? “The opportunity to compete on home waters (in the US) is amazing and it was definitely something that I was looking to do. However, … getting to be a part of the America’s Cup campaign, it’s kind of like a once in a lifetime opportunity that you don’t want to pass up. I’m definitely putting all my energy into this campaign at the moment.”

articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Rumesh Pathirage wins Asian Games javelin gold
articles.summary: Sri Lankan star ends incredible season with gold, while India’s Yashvir Singh and Rohit Yadav take silver and bronze.
articles.body:
Sri Lanka’s javelin star Rumesh Pathirage has continued his near-unbeaten streak this year by clinching gold at the Asian Games, as India’s Yashvir Singh and Rohit Yadav grabbed silver and bronze.

Pathirage topped the podium with 88.55m in his final throw on Monday, while Singh, who won bronze at the Commonwealth Games earlier this year, upgraded to silver with a personal best of 85.72m and Yadav took bronze with 84.35m.

Pakistan’s Olympic champion Arshad Nadeem could only muster 80.29m to finish fourth.

In an exclusive interview with Al Jazeera earlier this month, Pathirage said he was eyeing Nadeem’s Asian record of 92.97m set at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

World number one Pathirage got off to a shaky start with a dismal 73.53m — the only throw he’s had below 80m this season — before returning to form in the second round.

He then launched a massive 88.33m in his fourth throw to eclipse the Indian duo and all but secure his gold medal. A no-throw in his fifth attempt was bettered with 88.55m in his sixth to claim the continental crown.

The victory capped off an unprecedented season for Pathirage, who entered the Asian Games having won all but one of the competitions he’s contested this year.

Monday’s win was the final addition to his trophy cabinet with golds from the Commonwealth Games , the Diamond League final and the inaugural Ultimate Championships in Budapest.

Pathirage, 23, became the only thrower this season and fourth in history to breach the 92m mark in a year — a rare feat in javelin.

He catapulted to the top ranks when he threw a mammoth 92.62m at the Rome Diamond League in June, which became a new national record that still stands as the world lead this year. He then launched 92.07m to claim gold at the Zurich Diamond League in August.

In the women’s final, China’s 18-year-old Yan Ziyi obliterated the Games record of 66.09m with her first and only throw of 70.46m.

The teen sensation has enjoyed a breakout season that saw her break the Asian record in May by throwing 71.74m.

Like Pathirage, she has dominated javelin all year, save for the Ultimate Championships, where she managed a silver after retiring injured, while Japan’s Haruka Kitaguchi took the crown with a national record of 68.92m.

Kitaguchi could only muster 62.70m on her final attempt in Nagoya to finish with silver, while compatriot Sae Takemoto threw a season’s best 62.15m for bronze in front of the home crowd.

articles.title: De'Von Achane hurt: Jaylen Wright, Ollie Gordon, or none of the above?
articles.summary: De’Von Achane’s injury opens the door for RBs teammates Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon. Here's why fantasy managers should be wary of adding them.
articles.body:
De'Von Achane's injury opens the door for RB teammates Jaylen Wright and Ollie Gordon. Should managers grab one of them off waivers? There are key reasons not to.

Achane faced huge fantasy headwinds entering this season, making him a clear-cut fade at his RB6 / overall-11 ADP. In past years, he benefited from having Tyreek Hill and Jaylen Waddle at wideout. Achane found plenty of open space to operate, resulting in chunk runs and plenty of scoring opportunities.

His generous RB6 preseason ADP simply wasn't realistic. Sure enough, he encountered career lows in yards-before-first-contact, yards-after-first-contact, and broken-tackle rate. As the offensive centerpiece—rather than one part of a powerful trio—he was exposed by defenses that understood containing Achane was a key to victory.

His injury will turn Wright and Gordon into popular waiver adds. Jarquez Hunter or someone else on the practice squad could be elevated if Achane is sidelined. RB-needy managers might be desperate to add Wright and/or Gordon.

I would advise against it. Achane had the backfield largely to himself. Wright and Gordon probably would split touches, or else one would cap the other's ceiling. Also, this remains a below-average offense that will face plenty of negative game scripts, which generally aren't favorable for running backs.

Let an opponent claim one or more of these RBs. Save yourself the hassle of trying to guess who might get you 5+ points.

articles.title: Could Potter be England's next breakthrough star?
articles.summary: With Sarina Wiegman set to name her latest England squad on Tuesday, there is one name everyone is talking about - Lexi Potter. Here is why.
articles.body:
With Sarina Wiegman set to name her latest England squad on Tuesday, there is one name everyone is talking about.

The 20-year-old Chelsea midfielder has been a standout performer in the Women's Super League this season and has staked a claim to earn her first senior call-up.

After steady performances against Manchester United and Birmingham City, she caught everyone's attention with an impressive display against rivals Arsenal .

Potter helped Chelsea to a 1-0 victory and a third successive league clean sheet as she looked right at home among England's elite.

Former Lionesses striker Ellen White said Potter was "a special player", while Chelsea team-mate Lucy Bronze believed she could be the next Keira Walsh .

So why is everyone so excited about Potter and is she ready to join the England squad for the first time this week?

Potter's performance against Arsenal was the latest in a string of displays that have pleased manager Sonia Bompastor.

The Chelsea academy graduate broke through last season, scoring the winner on her first WSL start against Brighton in March.

It came after a two-year spell on loan at Crystal Palace where she gained regular first-team football and has already notched up 20 appearances.

This season Potter has stepped up, starting alongside England midfielder Walsh in three of Chelsea's four WSL matches.

Their partnership is flourishing and it has allowed Walsh to push further up the pitch and provide a goalscoring threat for the Blues.

Their winner against Arsenal came as a result of Walsh's saved shot falling to the feet of Alyssa Thompson , while Potter herself scored in the 2-0 victory over Birmingham.

When asked about Potter's impact, Bompastor said: "I was really happy with Lexi last season, though she probably didn't get as many opportunities as this season.

"For her age, being able to be consistent and in the way that she has been performing, I think it's great.

"People were probably looking at [the Arsenal game] to see her in a big occasion and whether she was able to repeat and sustain the performance.

"I think she proved that she can. Keira [Walsh] is playing at that level because she has more freedom to go forward by having Lexi next to her."

Potter has shown immense composure on the ball and maintained a 93% passing accuracy in the WSL so far this season.

She ranks fourth among her team-mates in tackles and interceptions and has the third-best passing success rate at Chelsea.

The midfielder has already played 207 minutes, made 21 recoveries in the WSL and is yet to be on the pitch while her side have conceded a goal this term.

"Chelsea have spent a lot of money on players in that team but she has grabbed the opportunity," ex-England striker White told the Women's Football Weekly podcast.

"It seems like she is really learning from Keira Walsh and players around her in the environment. She is growing game by game and has great physicality.

"There was one point in the Arsenal game where she had three players around her and she just flicked it around the corner to Ellie Carpenter .

"That's special to do when you're that age."

Potter has slotted into the number six position at Chelsea, provided defensive cover for Walsh and shown she can play her way out under pressure.

She has similar traits to Walsh, who has been a significant figure for England since her debut in 2017 and has over 100 caps for Wiegman's side.

One of the biggest questions surrounding Walsh has been whether anyone was capable of filling in her shoes when the 29-year-old eventually moves on.

Potter's emergence suggests she is next in line - but in the meantime, could she develop a successful partnership with Walsh in England's midfield?

"We have been crying out for someone who maybe is the next Keira Walsh. The number six position is a really difficult one to play in," added White.

"Keira has been doing it so well for so many years and is now getting better this season. She has stepped up and maybe Lexi is pushing her.

"To have Lexi in the England fold, gaining experience in the senior squad would be brilliant to see. She looks really special."

The Lionesses are hoping to secure qualification for next year's Women's World Cup in Brazil with a double-header against Greece in October.

After beating Arsenal, Chelsea boss Bompastor joked that she wished Potter could be French and believed she was ready for the international stage.

England defender Bronze, 34, added on BBC Radio 5 Live: "I'm not the manager and Sarina [Wiegman] will make her choices but Lexi has been absolutely fantastic.

"She was last year too. I remember my first season at Chelsea and seeing her train at the level she was...

"Having a player like Keira to look up to, and base her style off and learn from, you can see in every game they are developing into the same player.

"If England have another Keira Walsh, it puts us in a very good position!"

articles.title: Commanders’ Leo Chenal to miss remainder of season
articles.summary: Washington Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal left Sunday's game and will miss the remainder of the season with a neck fracture.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders got their first win of the season against the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 3, but they lost someone in the process. Linebacker Leo Chenal suffered a scary neck injury with just under seven minutes to play in the second quarter.

Seahawks running back Emmanuel Wilson was carrying the ball when Chenal tackled him short of the line to gain. Unfortunately, Chenal led with his head and appeared to jam his neck in the process. On replay, it looked almost more like a shoulder injury at first, but then the cart came out, and the seriousness of the injury became clear. Chenal was strapped down, but could be seen pumping his fist as the cart took him off the field.

Today, as injury reports are being released, we have learned that Chenal will miss the remainder of the 2026 season. He has a fracture in his neck that will require season-ending surgery.

Before his exit, Chenal recorded three tackles (two solo) and one tackle for a loss, but his stats aren't what the Commanders will miss the most. Chenal ranks second in tackles and was playing extremely well against the Seahawks when he got hurt. Chenal's injury leaves rookie Sonny Styles as the only healthy linebacker from the original top four. Frankie Luvu has missed two games with a hamstring injury, and backup Jordan Magee was placed on injured reserve after Week 1.

Second-year linebacker Kain Medrano capitalized on his first playing time on defense, returning a Sam Darnold interception 50 yards for a touchdown.

The good news is that despite his season being over, Chenal has full feeling and movement in his extremities, and he is expected to make a full recovery. In the meantime, the Commanders have to find a way to somehow mimic the impact Chenal had on the field. Chaisson started that against the Seahawks, but others will have to step up, too.

Commanders Wire sends its full support to Chenal and his family during this time. He will be missed, and we will welcome him back with open arms when he is ready to return to the field.

articles.title: Chicago Bears’ QB injury woes have team making desperation move for Week 3
articles.summary: A surprising name is expected to start for the Bears on Monday Night Football.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears host the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football in an early-season clash of NFC contenders. As expected, Ben Johnson's team must find a way to navigate the test without Caleb Williams after the quarterback suffered a grade 2 hamstring injury last Sunday against the Minnesota Vikings . What was initially feared to be a season-ending injury will only cause Williams to miss three or four weeks, which is good news for Chicago in the long term.

In the short term, finding a replacement for him has been a bit of a problem. Tyson Bagent , the Bears backup quarterback, suffered a concussion during his relief stint a week ago. Although he's officially cleared protocol, Chicago is expected to start third-stringer Case Keenum against the Eagles.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport has the latest:

From @GMFB : Case Keenum is expected to start tonight for the Bears, as QB3 takes center stage. pic.twitter.com/QberbM4zRS — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 28, 2026

From @GMFB : Case Keenum is expected to start tonight for the Bears, as QB3 takes center stage. pic.twitter.com/QberbM4zRS

Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 28, 2026

This is obviously not an ideal situation for the Bears. Philadelphia's defense is no picnic and falling to 1-2, while also trailing the tiebreaker with Minnesota, would not be a great recipe for success. Williams seems like he's going to be back sooner rather than later but there's always the chance it takes a bit for him to get back to full health.

Bagent has proven to be entirely serviceable in his short NFL career. It wasn't all that long ago that the fringier part of the Bears fanbase was pushing for him to start over Williams. To not have him out there will be a bummer.

To Keenum's credit he has put together a long and reasonably productive NFL career. Chicago is his eighth team in a 12-year career. He also hasn't started an NFL game since 2023 so things could go any number of ways in a standalone window with a lot of eyes watching.

articles.title: Florida just outside top 5 in USAT's Week 4 college football re-rank
articles.summary: Florida football's statement win over the Ole Miss Rebels in Week 4 has the Gators moving up into the top 10 of USA TODAY Sports' re-rank.
articles.body:
Florida football made a statement in Week 4 with a 52-28 victory over Ole Miss in the Swamp, improving to 4-0 for the first time since 2019.

The Gators tied the program record for most points scored against an AP Poll top-five team set in their 1997 Sugar Bowl victory over FSU for the national championship, while notching their first win against a top-five opponent since beating Georgia in 2020, snapping a 12-game losing streak.

Suffice it to say, the future looks bright for the Orange and Blue after the first four games of the Jon Sumrall era.

Following college football's fourth official week of play, USA TODAY Sports writer Paul Myerberg released his re-rank of all 138 FBS teams . In it, Florida leapt 11 spots and is now ranked just outside the top 5 at No. 6 — between No. 5 Ohio State and No. 7 Alabama.

Meanwhile, the Gators are ranked eighth in both the US LBM Coaches Poll and AP Top 25 — their highest ranking in both polls since 2021.

The SEC still has eight schools in USA TODAY Sports' re-rank top 25 this week, with top-ranked Georgia taking over the headline spot, along with Texas (No. 2), Florida (No. 6), Alabama (No. 7) and Ole Miss (No. 8) among the top 10. LSU (No. 13), Mississippi State (No. 16) and Tennessee (No. 18) round out the rest of the top-ranked teams.

Next up, Florida travels to Columbia to take on Missouri — who checks in at No. 29 in the re-rank — inside Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 3. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET and the game will be broadcast on ABC.
