articles.title: Kurt Warner's Theory on Why Buccaneers Are Struggling This Season
articles.summary: Kurt Warner has a theory on why the Tampa Bay Buccaneers are winless to start out the 2026 season
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are 0-3, and Kurt Warner has a theory on why they're struggling so much.

The Buccaneers dropped their third straight game in a loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 3, losing for the third consecutive time by one possession. The offense struggled to get going, scoring a season-low 16 points while averaging just 3.8 yards per play.

Kurt Warner, who is now an analyst after a Hall of Fame career as a star quarterback, has an idea of why Tampa Bay is struggling early in the season. While appearing on The Rich Eisen Show, Warner pointed to the departure and absence of Mike Evans as a key reason for Tampa Bay's struggles.

Warner points to Evans as being Baker Mayfield 's safety blanket, and now he's missing that for the first time this season.

"I think that's hurt them and Baker — to not have one guy to be able to go, 'Hey, this is the guy, my safety net, my safety blanket, that I can come back here and [throw to] this guy," Warner said.

Evans is the greatest receiver in franchise history and left for the San Francisco 49ers this offseason. The Buccaneers are averaging just 20.6 points per game and 279.3 total yards per game. Those are dips from last season when the offensive unit averaged 22.4 points and 320.4 total yards per game.

While Emeka Egbuka is certainly a star receiver and Chris Godwin remains a quality threat, it's clear the Buccaneers are missing the threat that Evans posed to opposing defenses. It's clear the offense has taken a step back, and the unit is struggling to create big plays without the presence of Evans.

It doesn't help matters that Mayfield suffered a thumb injury late in the Week 3 loss to the Vikings, which may sideline him for some time.

The Buccaneers will host the Green Bay Packers in Week 4 and could be eyeing a 0-4 start as they look for their first win of the season. Only seven teams in NFL history have started out 0-3 and made it to the playoffs.

articles.title: Best and worst PFF grades from Panthers' Week 3 loss to Browns
articles.summary: An unlikely Panthers WR stepped up in Week 3 and earned one of the team's top PFF grades. Here are the rest of the best (and worst) from Sunday...
articles.body:
With a chance to go into next week's prime-time showcase against the Detroit Lions atop their division at 2-1, the Carolina Panthers fell short. A dogfight against the Cleveland Browns here in Week 3 ended in a bitter 21-18 defeat , giving the reigning NFC South champs their second loss of the campaign.

There were certainly a fair amount of failures from the afternoon. Carolina did not win the war in the trenches, did not take advantage of potential takeaways and did not play the cleanest of games.

But at least the team did come away with a few encouraging performances.

Here are the Panthers' best and worst Pro Football Focus grades from Sunday . . .

Players listed recorded at least 10 offensive snaps or 10 defensive snaps.

Lewis was the only Panthers offensive lineman not to allow a pressure. He earned team-best grades in pass blocking (79.1) and run blocking (88.5).

Tremayne, with Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette sidelined, stepped up for a game-high 83 receiving yards on four grabs. Tremble and Evans pitched in with three receptions apiece, as the former went for 41 yards and the latter 36.

Young completed 26 of his 48 throws for 291 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He leads the NFL in passing yards (939) heading into the final game of the Week 3 slate.

It appears as though most of the offensive line struggled, no?

Hunt, Freeling and Walker each allowed six pressures. The lowest pass-blocking grade of the bunch belonged to Fortner (34.4).

Dodson tallied six tackles in his Panthers debut. He was also credited with three stops.

Brown picked up three stops as well to go along with a pair pressures.

Evans filled in quite admirably for Mike Jackson , who departed in the first quarter with a groin injury. He earned a team-best 78.1 grade in coverage.

Oh, well it appears as though the safeties also struggled, no?

Moehrig whiffed on three tackles. Ransom missed on two.

Umanmielen tied for the team-lead in pressures (five) with fellow starting outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips . But his coverage grade of 29.7 was, by far, the lowest on the defense.

articles.title: New Rumors Make Detroit Pistons Trading Jalen Duren This Week a Move That’s Best For Business
articles.summary: A pair of rumors make it seem like the Detroit Pistons trading Jalen Duren this week would be a move […]
articles.body:
A pair of rumors make it seem like the Detroit Pistons trading Jalen Duren this week would be a move that is now best for business.

The Pistons-Duren relationship has slowly deteriorated throughout the summer. He entered the offseason as a restricted free agent seeking a max contract from Detroit or another interested team. However, the Pistons have blocked all sign-and-trade discussions in the hopes of forcing the big man to sign their offer. As talks have dragged out, the club reportedly increased its recent offer to $200 million . Yet it still isn't enough for Duren.

Duren earned All-Star and All-NBA honors for the first time after a breakout season in 2025-26. He should have all the leverage in contract talks because he is a 22-year-old star big man on the rise. However, he doesn't because of an awful showing in the 2026 playoffs that cost the Pistons a trip to the Eastern Conference Finals for the first time in close to 20 years. It has emboldened Detroit to take a harder stance in negotiations.

Jalen Duren believes he can get a max contract next summer, and 2 teams are willing to give it to him

Yet, the center and his representatives aren't budging, and it is becoming realistic he will accept the team's $9.6 million qualifying offer so he can return to free agency next summer. This means the Pistons need to consider trading him instead of losing him for nothing in a year. But how likely is it that the All-Star leaves two hundred million on the table to spite Detroit? Well, it seems very likely.

"Per league sources, the Sacramento Kings and Milwaukee Bucks are known to be among the teams with serious interest in Duren. Both teams have veteran big men with strong resumes who could potentially fill the hole left by Duren in a deal, but the Pistons have refused to engage in talks on that front for months now," The Athletic reports.

"Per league sources, Duren believes he could land a maximum-salary deal next summer and eventually make up the money lost next season over the course of the next five years."

Is Jalen Duren taking Detroit Pistons qualifying offer realistic?

Nevertheless, the Pistons center would be taking a huge risk by not accepting the team's offer. He could either suffer a serious injury or not have quite as good a season in 2026-27 as he did last year. Yet, Duren taking the smaller qualifying offer is not that outlandish because another top free agent this summer seriously considered it.

According to Marc Stein, "league sources say that Walker Kessler 's camp successfully convinced Utah Jazz officials that he was absolutely determined to go the qualifying offer route this summer had he stayed in Utah and then proceeded to free agency next summer."

That threat compelled the Jazz to make a sign-and-trade with the Los Angeles Lakers that landed them two unprotected first-round picks and two first-round pick swaps.

If two young bigs with the chance to get huge pay increases are willing to take lower offers for a year so they can leave their current teams and go somewhere that will offer the money they want, the Pistons should stop playing with fire and consider trading Duren this week. Or risk having a disgruntled player on the roster all season who is looking to get numbers for a return to free agency next year.

articles.title: Kentucky rises in SEC power rankings after week four win
articles.summary: The Kentucky football team struggled early, but are 3-1 after week four, and continue to move up in the SEC power rankings.
articles.body:
Week four was one of moving upward for the Kentucky football team. Despite not playing their best early against South Alabama , they got the win, and moved up in the US LBM Coaches Poll , moved up into the top 25 in the AP Poll , and are moving up in this week's power rankings.

Early on, the Wildcats looked lethargic, and fell behind more than once against the Jaguars. The defense wasn't able to generate a pass rush, and got burned on some big plays, but they got a big turnover late and took a lead into halftime. In the second half, they took over with a dominant running game, and pulled ahead for a blowout victory.

Around the rest of the SEC, things were no less exciting. The Texas Longhorns and Tennessee Volunteers played a tight game that came down to the very end while Mississippi State and Missouri featured a fourth quarter comeback.

It's still early in the season, but the top teams of the SEC are beginning to announce themselves. Where does Kentucky fall in that pecking order at this point? Here are this week's conference power rankings.

Arkansas got a win this week, and certainly looked better than previous weeks. However, they need to do it against a power conference competition.

It got ugly quickly for the Sooners, who haven't found their stride this season. They're just 2-2 on the season, and that includes a win over New Mexico where they played poorly as well.

The Commodores suffered their first loss on Saturday, and the offense struggled to get going. The defense played well, and kept the in the game, though.

South Carolina ran into a red hot Alabama team, and got beaten in every way. The bigger concern is the state of the team after suspending their best defensive player.

A second straight loss has the Aggies reeling. They have loads of talent, but will only go as far as quarterback Marcel Reed can take them.

After a close win over Troy last week, the Tigers fell to Kamario Taylor and Mississippi State this week. Austin Simmons and the offense played well, but the defense just couldn't get enough stops.

The Tigers have been up and down this season, but held on for a win on Saturday. The defense was especially strong, and they didn't let Vandy's freshman QB get comfortable.

It was another slow start for the Wildcats, which is a concern going forward. Coach Will Stein was unhappy with their performance, and the pass rush has to be more consistent.

The Rebels had no answers for Florida on Saturday, giving up 52 points. Trinidad Chambliss did what he could, but they had a big letdown after an emotional win over LSU the week before.

Many people wondered just how good the Vols really were, and they held their own against the country's No. 1 team. They came up just short in an exciting, low-scoring game.

Kamario Taylor continues to be must-see TV, and led a come from behind victory on Saturday. The Bulldogs are going to give every team they play all they an handle.

It's hard to know what to make of LSU right now, but they bounced back quickly after losing to Ole Miss. They dominated the Aggies on Saturday.

The Gators faced a big test on Saturday and passed with flying colors. Jadan Baugh continues to put up huge numbers, and make his case for the Heisman Trophy.

Keelon Russell had his best game yet, and his continued development puts the Crimson Tide into the national championship race. They looked elite on Saturday.

The Bulldogs have dominated every team they've faced so far this season. It will be interesting to see them face better competition when the schedule ramps up.

The Longhorns already have two wins over ranked teams this season. It hasn't always been pretty, but they have earned the top spot here, and in the polls.

articles.title: Bengals snap counts: What’s going on with Shemar Stewart?
articles.summary: Where is Shemar Stewart for the Bengals?
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals fell to 2-1 with Sunday's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers .

Many deja-vu-inducing mistakes plagued the Bengals on the day, with the defense looking like its 2025 iteration, special teams looking lost and Joe Burrow committing a late turnover while trying to play hero ball.

One of the more notable things coming out of the loss, though, was how the defense split up the snap counts.

Perhaps the biggest thing that sticks out from the snap counts: Shemar Stewart didn't get one.

Now, there are some disclaimers here. Stewart grabbed a sack last week while playing just five snaps, but it was an easy one after others opened a path to the quarterback.

Stewart is also coming back from a knee injury, so load management is worth considering. And Cedric Johnson , who had been super productive on limited work so far, only had 12 snaps.

Those things aside, this isn't the sort of return the Bengals should be getting from a recent first-round pick. Cashius Howell, a second-round rookie, got 25 snaps (40 percent) in Pittsburgh.

It's not time to sound the alarm about Stewart. Some games, formations and matchups require different looks. He's coming back from injury. But at the same time, it would be unwise to ignore just how developmental of a prospect he really was and wonder why he can't jump up to being, say, the fourth edge in the rotation right now.

Big issue? Only if it continues. The Bengals are deep at the edge and it's a good thing. But there's that return-on-investment thing to keep in the back of the mind with high-end draft picks like this, too, so it's something to monitor.

articles.summary: After Florida State defeated the FCS Central Arkansas Bears on Saturday, are the Seminoles good enough to be ranked in the AP Top 25?
articles.body:
The Florida State Seminoles hosted the FCS Central Arkansas Bears and defeated them by a score of 34-7 on Saturday in Doak Campbell Stadium.

While FSU did not receive any votes in the AP Top 25 after Week 4, just two ACC teams are now ranked. The Miami Hurricanes are at No. 4 after beating Central Michigan 52-13. The SMU Mustangs are at No. 21. In addition, Duke, Wake Forest, Virginia Tech, Pittsburgh, and Louisville all find themselves in the "others receiving votes" category.

Texas still holds the No. 1 spot after defeating Tennessee at Neyland, 20-17. Georgia stays at No. 2, along with Notre Dame at No. 3. Miami rises two spots to No. 4 while Ohio State and Indiana round out the top six.

Bad news too, FSU fans: The Florida Gators are now No. 8. They rise 13 spots after crushing No. 4 Ole Miss in The Swamp.

FSU will look to try to upset the Virginia Cavaliers when they welcome them to Doak Campbell Stadium for the first time since 2014 on Saturday, Oct. 3 at 3:30 p.m. ET. The game will air on ESPN 2.

articles.title: British schoolgirl becomes chess’ youngest ever woman grandmaster
articles.summary: An 11-year-old chess prodigy has become the youngest woman grandmaster of all time, after a strong performance at the 46th Chess Olympiad.
articles.body: An 11-year-old chess prodigy has become the youngest woman grandmaster of all time, after a strong performance at the 46th Chess Olympiad. Bodhana Sivanandan from northwest London represented England at the tournament in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, which ended on Sunday. In an interview released on YouTube on Sunday, she told the International Chess Federation (FIDE) that she is keen to “keep making history.” Becoming a woman grandmaster means she has attained the highest female-only title in chess. “I’m happy to do it, but I want to keep going and keep making history as well, instead of just stopping here,” said Sivanandan, who previously became Britain’s youngest female chess champion and the youngest person to represent England at an international tournament in any sport. Asked whether she felt the pressure of playing on the top board at the tournament, Sivanandan said: “Not really, I just tried to enjoy it.” She explained that this was her second Olympiad. “It kind of felt very similar to the last one except I was playing on a different board,” she said. Asked about her love of chess, Sivanandan said she enjoyed the travel involved as well as the sport’s benefit to her school work. “It links to loads of school subjects so it’s really useful there as well,” she said. The latest tournament continues a meteoric rise for Sivanandan, who became the youngest female player to defeat a grandmaster in August 2025. She beat 60-year-old grandmaster Pete Wells at the age of just 10 years, five months and three days, breaking a record set by American Carissa Yip, who was 10 years, 11 months and 20 days old when she defeated a grandmaster in 2019, according to FIDE. In 2024, Sivanandan’s father told the BBC that “nobody at all” in their family had previously excelled at chess. Sivanandan said she picked up the sport during the Covid pandemic when she was five, after one of her dad’s friends gave the family some toys and books. “In one of the bags, I saw a chessboard, and I was interested in the pieces,” she told the BBC. “I wanted to use the pieces as toys. Instead, my dad said that I could play the game, and then I started from there.”

articles.title: MLB Postseason 2026: Does regular-season momentum matter in the playoffs?
articles.summary: Eric Samulski digs into whether or not data suggests teams can really "stumble" into the playoffs
articles.body:
Every October, some version of the same take can be heard in all playoff discussions: the team stumbling into the playoffs is doomed, and the team on a roll is a lock to advance. It sounds right. We believe that momentum is a real thing in sports. It makes sense to us that a team playing confidently in September should carry that into the postseason, and a team scuffling through the stretch run would carry that baggage along with it.

I pulled every MLB playoff team from the last nine full seasons (2016 through 2025, skipping the COVID-shortened 2020 season). That gave me 98 "seasons" using two different playoff formats. For each team and year, I pulled stats to show "how good was their September." For that, I decided to use both winning percentage and their team OPS that month. Then also pulled stats to show "how did they fare in the postseason?" For that, I used the round they were eliminated in, as well as their overall postseason winning percentage. After doing that, I cross-referenced the numbers to see if there was any connection.

These correlations are represented through a Pearson correlation, which I just learned about this week. It's basically a measure of how closely two things move together. In this case, 1.0 would mean September winning percentage and playoff success are perfectly linked, and 0 would mean they have nothing to do with each other. When I compared September winning percentage to playoff advancement, I got a score of 0.020, which is essentially zero. There was no connection.

I then checked September winning percentage against postseason winning percentage and got 0.004. Even less of a connection than to playoff advancement. I then checked September team OPS to playoff round reached and got 0.186, which was a little better, but still not great. Lastly, I checked September OPS against playoff winning percentage and got 0.052. All of which is to say, however you slice it, a team's September tells you almost nothing about what its October will look like.

One way to determine who "did well" in the playoffs is to see who advanced the farthest. If momentum truly mattered, then we'd expect the two teams that made it to the World Series to be teams that were playing well to end the year. Instead, the nine World Series matchups show no real connection to September success. Some World Series participants had September OPSs as high as .882 (2019 Astros), and some were as low as .696 (2024 Yankees ). In fact, six of the 18 participants had truly poor September OPS marks under .740. The 2022 Astros still won the whole thing.

The best example of how September performance doesn't correlate is the 2023 Diamondbacks. They reached the World Series despite having the single worst September OPS of any of the 12 playoff teams that year. Back in 2017, the Dodgers had the 9th-best OPS of the 10 playoff teams in September, with an 11th-percentile finish to the regular season, and still won the NL pennant. The 2021 Braves won the whole thing with the worst September OPS of any NL team at .766; that was a 22nd percentile OPS in all of baseball that month.

If we look at the inverse and assume early exits were limited to poor September teams, we would also be wrong. Of the nine champions in this little study, only four actually rode really above-average Septembers to a title: the 2019 Nationals, the 2023 Rangers, and the 2024 and 2025 Dodgers. There just doesn't appear to be any throughline here.

The Cold Teams That Got Hot at the Right Time

If we were to expand beyond just the teams that made the World Series, we see more examples of how a bad September wasn't actually a red flag.

The 2025 Tigers are the extreme case. They finished September with a record of 7-17. That's a .292 winning percentage that is, by far, the worst September of any playoff team in nine years I looked at. Yet, they still won their Wild Card series and advanced to the Division Series. The 2024 Royals weren't much better by OPS, posting a .577 mark that's the lowest of any playoff team in this entire sample, and they also won their first playoff series.

The 2022 Phillies might be a useful comparison for a few teams in the 2026 postseason, like, say, the 2026 Phillies. The 2022 team limped into October with a 11-14 record in September. They have a below-average but not brutal OPS yet still had one of the worst records in that year's playoff field. Yet, they just kept winning and made the World Series. Could we see something similar for the 2026 Phillies, Cubs, or Red Sox ? Three teams that had been pretty strong for most of the season (OK, late June on for Boston ) but struggled with poor finishes to the season?

The other half of the argument is perhaps more surprising, because it's the situation that the "backing in" theory says shouldn't happen. Many teams that were rolling right into the playoffs still lost their very first series.

The 2021 Cardinals are the best example. They finished the regular season with a 22-7 month of September. Their .759 winning percentage is the third-best in the entire nine-year dataset. They also backed that up with a strong .799 team OPS, which was 67th percentile among that year's playoff field. All of that earned them one game: a 3-1 loss to the Dodgers in the single-elimination Wild Card round. (Yes, perhaps that's an example of why the three-game series makes some sense).

The 2022 Blue Jays team makes the same point, mostly. Yes, Toronto 's 18-10 record wasn't as impressive as St. Louis ', but it wsa a strong mark, and the Blue Jays also had a .804 team OPS in September, which was the single best mark of any playoff team that year. Still, the Blue Jays were swept out of the Wild Card round in two games, losing to the Mariners 4-0 and 10-9.

A few more examples listed above: the 2017 Twins (.805 OPS, 78th percentile) and the 2018 A's (.800 OPS, also 78th percentile) both turned strong Septembers into first-round exits. The Twins lost 8-4 to the Yankees, while the A's actually did this in back-to-back years. The 2018 A's were 97-65 and had a great September, but lost 7-2 to the Yankees in the Wild Card round, and the 2019 A's were also 97-65 (yes, for real), and took an even stronger September into a 5-1 loss to the Rays .

So What Does September Actually Tell Us?

Not much, at least not about October. The best explanation isn't that momentum doesn't exist. Teams clearly can and do get hot or cold in ways that we can see with our own eyes. Just think about the New York Knicks' NBA title run a few months ago. However, what we can say is that a 25-or-30-game sample in September doesn't predict a short playoff series decided by small details like what starting pitcher is lined up, which bullpen is more effective, which manager makes the better pinch-hit decision, and myriad other small decisions that impact a baseball game.

And what does this mean for the 2026 postseason?

Well, obviously, nothing. Any of these teams could go on a run, but it's smarter to favor season-long success over September success. That means teams like the Cubs, who had the best wRC+ in baseball this season, or the Dodgers, who were second in both wRC+ and OPS, stand a better chance of making a deep run than the Padres, who had the best record in September and were second in wRC+, or the Guardians, who finished with a .640 winning percentage in September, the fifth-best in the league.

Of course, teams like the Dodgers and Brewers have been atop the leaderboards in September and also in season-long leagues, which is often the best indicator of a team that is truly built to make a deep playoff run.

articles.title: MLB playoff schedule 2026: Full bracket, scores, times, TV channels to watch every postseason series
articles.summary: The 2026 MLB postseason will unwind across a month of action to determine a champion. Here's when and where to watch every game.
articles.body:
More than seven months after pitchers and catchers reported to spring training, it's time to determine which team will wear the MLB crown in 2026.

Twelve teams reached the postseason bracket, and any discussion about favorites has to start with the two-time defending champion Dodgers . Los Angeles wasn't necessarily dominant during the regular season and enters October with concerns about the health of the planet's best player, Shohei Ohtani , but it has proven unwise to bet against LA lately.

While the Dodgers are in the midst of a dynastic run, neither of the teams that owned the best records in their respective leagues during the regular season — the Brewers and Rays — has won a World Series. Victory would be particularly sweet for either of those fan bases, along with the other postseason entrant without a title, the Padres.

Who will survive the gauntlet to lift the Commissioner's Trophy at the end of October? Here's when and where to watch every game.

The 2026 MLB postseason will have a new look for the opening round, with NBC carrying every wild card game on its platforms: NBC, NBCSN and/or Peacock .

After that, the familiar rotation returns. This year's NL playoffs will air on Fox or FS1 while the AL will be on TBS, with the World Series set to air on Fox as it has every year since 2000.

Fans can stream every postseason game except Peacock exclusives with DIRECTV , which offers a free trial to new subscribers.

All games airing on NBC, NBCSN, Fox and FS1 can be streamed with fubo , which also offers a free trial.

articles.title: Valkyries news: Gabby Williams' plan to slow down Paige Bueckers in Game 2
articles.summary: Paige Bueckers was nearly perfect in her WNBA playoff debut during the Dallas Wings’ Game 1 against the Golden State Valkyries. But the Bay Area forward Gabb...
articles.body:
Paige Bueckers was nearly perfect in her WNBA playoff debut during the Dallas Wings ' Game 1 against the Golden State Valkyries . But the Bay Area forward Gabby Williams believes the best way to handle her is to make every possession physically demanding.

Bueckers scored 21 points on 9-of-10 shooting in Game 1, but the Valkyries still cruised to a 104-80 win over the Dallas Wings at Chase Center.

Williams spent much of the night defending Bueckers and knows completely shutting down an elite scorer isn't realistic. Instead, the two-time WNBA All-Star plans to make Bueckers work for every shot and trust that the physical pressure will eventually take its toll.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"She's obviously an excellent player, one of the best in our league," Williams said. "I just want to make everything difficult. Obviously, she hit almost all of her shots today, but as long as I can make them hard, tough shots, where she has to really work for them, and then she gets tired, that's just kind of the goal."

While Bueckers was impressive individually, Golden State's help defense limited the rest of Dallas' offense. The Wings shot just 30% from three-point range, while Jessica Shepard was held scoreless on 0-of-4 shooting.

Williams finished Game 1 with 20 points, four assists and three rebounds in 27 minutes. Bueckers added six rebounds and two assists but finished with a minus-23 rating.

The Valkyries now lead the best-of-three series 1-0 and can advance to the semifinals with another win Wednesday. Game 2 will take place at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, on September 30, with tip-off scheduled for 8:00 p.m. ET.

articles.title: NBC rules analyst: Refs blew critical call in Rams-Broncos
articles.summary: Sunday night’s wild showdown between the Los Angeles Rams and Denver Broncos came down to the final play, with Denver pulling out a come-from-behind 30-26 wi...
articles.body:
Sunday night's wild showdown between the Los Angeles Rams and Denver Broncos came down to the final play, with Denver pulling out a come-from-behind 30-26 win. Former NFL ref and current NBC rules analyst Terry McAulay believes the Broncos were aided by an officiating miscue on their previous possession.

Trailing 26-23 and facing 3rd-and-6 from the Rams' 11-yard line with 1:15 to play, Broncos quarterback Bo Nix was intercepted by Los Angeles ' Josh Wallace , seemingly sealing the victory for the visitors. However, Wallace was called for a controversial defensive pass interference penalty, which extended the drive and led to Nix's game-winning touchdown run moments later.

On the broadcast, McAulay, who worked in the NFL from 1998-2017, made it clear he didn't think Wallace interfered with Broncos wide receiver Pat Bryant .

"As we get towards the end, we actually see the receiver grab the defender and pull in on him," McAulay said. "I don't see the defender do anything that significantly hinders the receiver on this play."

"Even the first part of it when he contacts Bryant?" asked play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico.

"Even the first part. There's just hands on him, he doesn't do anything with them," McAulay responded.

McAulay also said he believed the play should have been ruled an interception.

"If the knee gets down, yes. If two feet are down, yes. I absolutely—that's what I see," he explained, to which game analyst Cris Collinsworth agreed."

Rams head coach Sean McVay said postgame he believed Wallace's coverage "looked like it was a good, competitive play from my vantage point."

As for Wallace, who recorded an interception earlier in the contest, he didn't have much to say about the penalty when asked.

"It's tough," Wallace said . "I felt like we stopped them a couple of times. Just got to keep playing at the end of the day."

The Broncos moved to 2-1 on the season while the Rams fell to 1-2.

articles.title: Bob Chesney and the Bruins had their first truly dominant showing
articles.summary: The UCLA Bruins continue to surpass expectations during the 2026 season. UCLA is now the No. 23 team in the country.
articles.body:
Things continue to go to plan for Bob Chesney and the UCLA Bruins . UCLA now finds themselves as a Top-25 team in the nation just four games into Chesney's tenure, with the team being 4-0 heading into their Week 6 meeting with the Oregon Ducks .

It took big fourth quarters for UCLA to capture their first three wins of the season but that changed on Saturday. The Bruins dominated throughout, picking up a 54-3 win on the East Coast against Maryland .

Chesney and the Bruins are turning heads. Trojans Wire writer Matt Zemek is among those impressed by UCLA's first-year head coach.

"Bob Chesney watched his UCLA defense allow 38 points at home to Purdue. His own team scored 52, so it didn't matter in terms of a win or loss, but it mattered to Vegas. UCLA was a tiny 1.5-point favorite according to the sportsbooks because the Bruins, though unbeaten, did not demolish opponents," Zemek said. "They needed a big fourth quarter to pull away from a Cal team which we can see is not very good. They were stuck in mud for two and a half quarters against San Diego State before finally busting loose to win. They allowed 38 to Purdue. The Bruins were winning but not dominating. That all changed against Maryland."

It was a statement win for the program, proving that they're capable of strong-arming other Big Ten teams. UCLA also continued to prove that they're a top tier rushing offense, putting up another game with over 200 rushing yards.

"This was total and sustained dominance. This was UCLA playing a road Big Ten game and delivering a knockout punch. Contrast this road Big Ten attitude and performance with crosstown rival USC, which has noticeably struggled on the road in the Big Ten throughout the Lincoln Riley era," Zemek said. "Beating Maryland was good. Blowing out Maryland should get everyone's attention. Bob Chesney looks like The Man. Nothing would suggest he isn't the exact leader UCLA football has needed."

UCLA will have next weekend off before the 2026 season resumes in Eugene, Oregon for a Week 6 showdown with No. 15 Oregon.

After another wild week of the high school soccer season, it's time to look back on the best performances.

Read about the players who stood out last week and let us know who you think should be the HSS North Jersey Player of the Week in the poll at the bottom of this page.

Baer made 26 saves and allowed one goal in two division wins last week, including a 17-save shutout against Demarest in a 1-0 victory that put the Tigers in first place. Ranked No. 1 in the Big North in saves, Baer is a key reason for Tenafly's hot start after graduating its entire starting defense.

Matthew Brooks, River Dell junior goalie

Brooks recorded two shutouts and made 25 saves last week, helping River Dell earn road victories over Mahwah and Ridgefield Park. The Golden Hawks are now 4-2 after finishing with six wins last year.

Kim recorded four goals and four assists in two wins last week, including his first career hat trick against Waldwick, as Glen Rock remained unbeaten and atop the NJIC Colonial. Kim now has 11 goals this season after totaling six during his first three varsity seasons.

Will Raman, Northern Highlands senior midfielder

Raman scored three goals and two assists in three wins, including a 2-0 victory over No. 2 Ramsey. The captain set up the game-clinching goal against Ramsey and sunk the winner against Pascack Hills as the Highlanders extended their winning streak to five games.

Madisyn Abella, Immaculate Heart junior forward

Abella helped the Blue Eagles cruise past a pair of ranked opponents last week, picking up six goals and one assist overall. She set a career-high by scoring four times against Bergen Tech.

Illuzzi continues to be one of the top scorers in the NJIC after lifting her team past Lodi and Weehawken. She combined for eight goals and one assist over two matches.

Pothos powered the offense with back-to-back hat tricks in wins over Northern Highlands and Teaneck. She finished with six goals and three assists for the week.
